title: CMA CGM completes $1.4 billion purchase of FedEx Supply Chain
sum: CMA CGM Group completed its acquisition of FedEx Supply Chain from FedEx Corp. for an enterprise value of $1.4 billion, according to Logistics Manager. CMA CGM and FedEx also executed multi-year commercial agreements covering ocean and air freight.

why: The deal nearly triples CEVA's North American contract logistics footprint and ties CMA CGM to FedEx through ocean and air freight agreements.

The purchase nearly triples the North American contract logistics footprint of CMA CGM's logistics subsidiary, CEVA Logistics, adding about 34 million square feet of warehouse space across 150 facilities. CMA CGM becomes a preferred non-exclusive ocean carrier for FedEx, and the companies plan an air freight capacity-sharing agreement on long-haul lanes such as Asia–Europe.

He calls for auditing rights, independent billing verification and ongoing review of carrier charges.

title: FedEx faces 13 consolidated tariff class actions in Memphis
sum: Thirteen proposed class actions over duties and tariff-related charges FedEx billed on imported shipments are combined as In re FedEx Tariff Litigation in the Western District of Tennessee, according to a class action news site. The plaintiffs' consolidated complaint is proposed for Nov. 4, 2026, with FedEx's response proposed for Dec. 4. The allegations are unproven and no class has been certified.

According to the article, FedEx has not been found liable, no class is certified and there is no settlement or claim form. Separately, FedEx has said it will pass IEEPA refunds it receives from the government to the customers who paid.

title: USPS audit finds Mail Recovery Center returned under 1% of items
sum: An audit by the USPS Office of Inspector General found the Postal Service's Mail Recovery Center returned less than 1% of items it received to customers, against management's reported 39%. Heidi Einsweiler, the OIG's Director of Sales, Marketing and International Mail Audits, said the agency lost about $109 million in a little over two years on returned packages that warehouses refused and did not pay postage for.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. Einsweiler said USPS is evaluating automatic collection from the original shipper and a cost-benefit analysis of disposal fees.
why: USPS is weighing automatic charges to the original label buyer and disposal fees for undeliverable packages, which could reach commercial shippers.
syn: A USPS Office of Inspector General audit of the Mail Recovery Center, which handles undeliverable packages the Postal Service calls dead mail, found management reported returning about 39% of items to customers while the actual figure was less than 1%. Einsweiler, the OIG's Director of Sales, Marketing and International Mail Audits, said a faulty weight-based estimate understated package volume by about four times, and that spreadsheet errors caused double counting. She also said USPS lost about $109 million in a little over two years because warehouses listed as return addresses refused items and postage, and USPS had no way to charge the shipper who bought the label. According to Einsweiler, USPS is evaluating auto-collection methods and disposal fees.

sum: Helaine Rich, vice president of strategic sales & administration at ePost Global, argues in an opinion piece that tariff and customs changes are raising the cost of cross-border returns. She also points to the next phase of the EU's customs reform on November 1 and says merchants that refund duties and taxes pay them twice when a product crosses a border again. title: Lowe's starts drone delivery pilot near Charlotte with DoorDash and Wing
sum: Lowe's has launched a drone delivery pilot at its Matthews, N.C., store through DoorDash and Wing, the company said. Select products can reach DIY and Pro customers in as fast as 20 minutes, with Wing drones carrying orders of about 2.5 pounds per flight.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Customers near the Matthews, N.C., store can order select small items through the DoorDash app.
why: A home improvement retailer is testing drone delivery of small items, adding to retail drone programs that carry roughly 2.5 pounds per flight.

title: CBP extends postal formal-entry compliance date to Jan. 20, 2027
sum: U.S. Customs and Border Protection extended the compliance date for formal entry of certain international postal shipments from Oct. 22, 2026 to Jan. 20, 2027, according to a final rule published in the Federal Register (91 FR 66638). It covers mail subject to partner government agency requirements, mail subject to duties under HTSUS Chapter 98 or 99, and mail claiming duty-free treatment under Chapter 98 or a free trade agreement. CBP said importers, brokers and logistics providers need more time to update systems and procedures.
plain: The formal-entry requirement for these categories of postal goods now applies from Jan. 20, 2027 instead of Oct. 22, 2026. CBP said the process for informal mail entries under the June 24, 2026 interim final rule does not change during the delay.
why: The delay gives importers, brokers and logistics providers in the international postal network until Jan. 20, 2027 to comply with the formal-entry requirement for these goods.
tie: CBP on Oct. 8, 2026 proposed earlier filing deadlines for low-value imports and more data for postal entries.

title: Stord acquires AMS Fulfillment, adding 10 million annual orders
sum: Stord, a fulfillment and commerce technology company, has acquired third-party logistics provider AMS Fulfillment in its largest acquisition to date and its 12th overall. Stord said the deal adds more than 10 million annual orders and facilities in the Los Angeles, Salt Lake City and Philadelphia areas, taking its network to more than 100 locations. Terms were not disclosed in the articles.
plain: No change to carrier rates or fees. AMS customers are expected over time to gain access to Stord's wider fulfillment network and parcel program, according to Stord.
why: Adds more than 10 million annual orders and over 1 million sq ft to a 3PL network that Stord says reaches one in four US households.
tie: Stord's October 2026 $400 million credit facility led by Citi and its May 2026 $250 million Series F round, which valued it at $3 billion, preceded the deal.

title: UPS completes automation of 4 more sortation facilities before peak
sum: UPS said it has converted four conventional package sortation centers into automated facilities, in Denver, St. Paul, Syracuse and Portland, ahead of the holiday peak. The company also said it is hiring 100,000 seasonal employees nationwide. FreightWaves reported the details from a UPS news release.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service terms was announced. UPS temporarily closed its Portland facility on Swan Island during construction and shifted operations to other locations.
why: UPS says automated sites cost about 28% less per piece, and 68.5% of its U.S. volume now moves through automated facilities, so network changes shape its cost base.

title: Amazon, Teamsters dig in over NYC Delivery Protection Act, Intro. 518
sum: The Queens Chronicle reported that supporters and opponents of the City Council's Delivery Protection Act (Intro. 518) have hardened positions. The bill, submitted by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán in February, would require a city permit for some last-mile delivery facilities and set safety, training and employment requirements. A Council Speaker spokesman said it is moving through the legislative process.
plain: No change to rates or service yet; the bill has not passed. If enacted as written, it would require permits for some NYC last-mile facilities and make the facility operator responsible for employing delivery workers.
why: The bill would make facility operators such as Amazon responsible for employing delivery workers, and Amazon says it affects more than 40 DSPs and 5,000 employees in the city.
new: The Chronicle reports both sides digging in, with Amazon citing more than 40 DSPs and 5,000 employees at risk and a source saying Amazon rejected rewritten versions; no change for shippers yet since the bill has not advanced to a vote.

title: USPS says it is set for 2026 holiday peak after 2.5-day 2025 average
sum: The Postal Service said on Oct. 22, 2026 that it is prepared for the holiday season, citing 673 package sorting machines added over six years, 164 of them this year. USPS said mail and packages were delivered in 2.5 days on average in the 2025 peak, versus 2.8 days a year earlier. It plans to hire a little more than 10,000 seasonal employees.
plain: No change to rates or fees was announced. USPS said Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express keep their stated delivery windows, with $100 insurance and tracking included on most shipments.
why: USPS says peak volumes rise about 40 percent between Oct. 1 and Dec. 31, so its capacity and delivery-time claims bear on shippers using Ground Advantage and Priority Mail.

title: MassDOT says Amazon has not applied for Westborough drone pad certificate
sum: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation told Amazon in an Oct. 22 letter that it needs a certificate of approval from its Aeronautics Division to open a Prime Air drone takeoff and landing area in Westborough or elsewhere in the state. The division said it has received no official notification or request for review from Amazon, and that Amazon should expect at least one public hearing before a decision.
plain: No change to rates or service. Amazon's Prime Air drone operations in Westborough, Massachusetts cannot begin until MassDOT issues a certificate, according to the letter.
why: Shows state approval is required before Amazon's planned Westborough drone site can operate; the letter ties this to Part 135 status.
tie: The letter follows an Oct. 19 request from 16 Massachusetts legislators for a freeze on drone delivery certificate applications, which responded to Amazon's plan to fly Prime Air drones from its Westborough warehouse.
new: MassDOT's letter states Amazon has submitted no notification or review request, cites § 39B and Part 135 status as the basis for requiring a certificate, and says at least one public hearing should be expected; no change to current shipper rates or service.

Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the division has received no official notification or request for review from Amazon, and that at least one public hearing should be expected before any decision. The letter cites M.G.L. c. 90, § 39B and says Amazon's FAA Part 135 approval makes its proposed operations commercial flights subject to that section. Amazon had told a Westborough audience on Sept. 23 that it planned to launch possibly by the end of October, per DroneXL.

title: Teamsters rally at City Hall for NYC Delivery Protection Act vote
sum: The Teamsters, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and other elected officials rallied at New York City Hall on Oct. 22, 2026, urging Council Speaker Julie Menin to schedule a vote on the Delivery Protection Act. The bill, authored by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán, would require delivery companies such as Amazon to register facilities with the city and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs. The Teamsters said Amazon has spent over $8 million against the bill.
plain: No change to rates or service yet; the bill has not been scheduled for a vote. If passed, it would require facility registration and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs.
why: The bill would ban subcontracted last-mile drivers in the five boroughs, which would affect how delivery companies like Amazon staff New York City routes.
new: The Teamsters held a City Hall rally on Oct. 22 with Mayor Mamdani and said Amazon has spent over $8 million against the bill; the vote has still not been scheduled, so nothing changes for shippers yet.

They urged Council Speaker Julie Menin to schedule a vote on the Delivery Protection Act. The bill, authored by Councilmember Tiffany Cabán, would require delivery companies like Amazon to register facilities with the city and ban subcontracting for last-mile drivers in the five boroughs. The Teamsters said a majority of the Council and the mayor support it and that Amazon has spent over $8 million against it.

title: MassDOT says Amazon needs state approval for Westborough drones
sum: The MassDOT Aeronautics Division told Amazon on Oct. 22 that it cannot launch Prime Air drone deliveries from Westborough, Massachusetts, without a state certificate of approval. Aeronautics Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the division has received no notification or request for review from Amazon. The Town of Berlin posted the letter.
plain: Amazon cannot start Prime Air drone deliveries from its Westborough fulfillment center until the state grants a certificate. No delivery service has changed yet.
why: A state certificate requirement stands between Amazon and a Westborough drone launch, with 16 communities expected to be affected.
new: Massachusetts regulators told Amazon on Oct. 22 that it needs a state certificate before flying from Westborough, adding a state-level step that no earlier coverage mentioned and leaving the Westborough launch without a start date.

Administrator Denise Garcia wrote that the FAA's Part 135 air carrier approval makes the flights commercial operations under state law. The division must complete a suitability review, and expects at least one public hearing before acting. Local steps are also underway, including a town bylaw vote and pending zoning and planning board hearings.

title: MassDOT tells Amazon to get review before Westborough drone ops
sum: The Massachusetts Department of Transportation sent Amazon a letter on Thursday saying its Aeronautics Division must complete a suitability review before any drone operations begin in Westborough, according to The Boston Globe. Amazon had originally planned to start in October from a parking lot at its Westborough Fulfillment Center, with deliveries of packages under 5 pounds within a 7.5-mile radius.
plain: No change to rates or service for current shippers. Amazon's planned Westborough drone launch cannot begin until the state completes its review, and the company had originally targeted October.
why: The state review could delay one Amazon Prime Air launch site, where drones would serve a 7.5-mile radius for packages under 5 pounds.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from sites near Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland and Syracuse, N.Y.
new: MassDOT told Amazon it must complete an Aeronautics Division suitability review before operating in Westborough, which was originally planned to start in October, adding a state-level approval step for that site only.

title: Deposco: Q3 carrier rates fall 3.3% per package, operator costs fall 0.6%
sum: Deposco published its Q3 2026 Commerce Signal report on Oct. 21, saying carrier rates fell 3.3% per package from Q2 while what operators paid declined 0.6%. The company said heavier packages, faster services and more residential deliveries absorbed most of the rate relief.
plain: Deposco says shippers' actual per-package spend fell far less than carrier rates in Q3 because of package mix. The report says peak surcharges begin Oct. 25 and expects per-package costs to rise in peak season.
why: Deposco's data suggests lower carrier rates did not carry through to what operators paid, and the report expects peak per-package costs to exceed Q3.

title: Pakistan arrests man over $126M counterfeit USPS label scheme
sum: Pakistan's cybercrime agency arrested Faheem Akram, 33, of Khanewal, accused of running LabelsBank.com, which allegedly sold counterfeit USPS shipping labels to US customers since 2023. US authorities said a Florida federal grand jury indicted him last month and that the scheme caused about $126 million in losses to USPS.
plain: No change to rates or service. The case concerns counterfeit postage sold to US customers, and the website has been shut down.
why: The case involves more than five million counterfeit labels and about $126 million in reported USPS losses, with over 5,200 buyers identified.

title: Mass. lawmakers seek drone delivery moratorium over Amazon plan
sum: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators sent a letter to Gov. Maura Healey, Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll and Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell asking for a task force on commercial delivery drone rules. They also asked for a moratorium on processing commercial drone delivery operator certificates until a review is done. The letter responds to Amazon Prime Air's proposed expansion centered on Westborough, according to the Franklin Observer.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon's proposed drone delivery from Westborough still faces local zoning review, and the lawmakers' requests are not binding on the state.
why: The request targets state oversight of drone takeoff and landing sites, which could affect Amazon's planned first New England drone hub in Westborough.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.
new: State legislators in Massachusetts asked the governor for a task force and a moratorium on drone operator certificates, and Amazon's Westborough site awaits a Zoning Board of Appeals review, so a planned New England launch may be delayed.

title: Kohl's adds Uber Eats, DoorDash and Instacart same-day delivery for holidays
sum: Kohl's said at an Oct. 21 media briefing that it is live with Instacart and DoorDash and will launch with Uber Eats in November. Chief customer officer Arianne Parisi said about 80% of these partners' same-day customers are new to Kohl's.
plain: No change to carrier rates or service. Kohl's customers get same-day delivery through DoorDash and Instacart now, and through Uber Eats from November.
why: A large retailer is adding three same-day delivery apps for peak; Kohl's says over 50% of holiday digital orders are touched by a store.

title: Pakistan court remands suspect in alleged $126 million USPS label fraud
sum: A judicial magistrate in Lahore on Wednesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency five-day physical remand of a 33-year-old suspect, Dawn reported. A Florida jury charged him with defrauding the US Postal Service of $126 million through the online sale of counterfeit postage labels, the US Attorney's Office of the Southern District of Florida said on Sept 28.
plain: No change to USPS rates or service. The case concerns counterfeit postage labels sold through a website that was not authorised to sell USPS products; a US court order authorised its seizure and shutdown.
why: US prosecutors say counterfeit labels sold at about $2 each caused USPS losses above $126 million.

title: Jefferies: Amazon automation, parcel network could lift margins
sum: Jefferies said Amazon's warehouse automation and expanding logistics network could strengthen retail margins, following a discussion with a logistics industry expert. The broker said Amazon could grow US delivery stations from about 575 to 950 by 2030 and handle more third-party parcels now carried by UPS and the US Postal Service. Early trials reportedly show 20% to 25% savings for business-to-consumer shippers.
plain: No change to Amazon's rates or service is announced; this is a broker's view of possible growth. Jefferies said early trials show lower costs for some B2C shippers, partly because Amazon avoids some residential, weekend and package surcharges, and that peak-season execution remains a test.
why: Jefferies says Amazon's third-party parcel delivery could take volume from UPS and USPS, with early trials reportedly saving B2C shippers 20% to 25%.

title: Wing and Walmart launch drone delivery from 7 Charlotte-area stores
sum: Wing announced on Oct. 21 that it and Walmart now fly drone deliveries from seven Walmart Supercenters around Charlotte, N.C., with two more Charlotte stores due within a week. Orders of groceries, household goods and over-the-counter medicine can arrive in as little as 30 minutes for customers within about 6 miles of a participating store. The Charlotte stores are part of 60 Walmart stores nationwide offering the service, toward a target of more than 270 by the end of 2027.
plain: Customers within about 6 miles of the seven participating Charlotte-area Walmart stores can order by drone through the Walmart app, Walmart.com or the Wing app. Orders are capped at 2.5 pounds, and Business North Carolina reports delivery is now free.
why: Walmart's drone service is at 60 stores nationwide, toward a target of more than 270 by the end of 2027.
tie: Wing and Walmart said in October 2026 they would add Denver and Seattle drone delivery in 2027, with Charlotte counted among Wing's five flying metros at that time.
new: Wing consolidated seven Charlotte-area Walmart stores into one metro service on Oct. 21, with two more due within a week, giving shippers in range a drone option with a 2.5-pound order cap and, per Business North Carolina, no delivery fee.

title: Over a third of self-employed UK parcel drivers say pay is below minimum wage
sum: University of Sheffield researchers said more than a third of self-employed delivery drivers believe their hourly pay is below the national minimum wage. The survey covered more than 1,400 parcel delivery drivers across the UK. The researchers also reported intense digital monitoring and weaker employment protections.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report describes pay and working conditions of UK parcel delivery drivers.
why: The survey of more than 1,400 UK parcel drivers compares pay, breaks and costs for self-employed and directly employed drivers in the delivery workforce.

title: Amazon plans 300,000 holiday hires, up from 250,000 last year
sum: Amazon said Oct. 20 it plans to hire more than 300,000 workers for the holiday season, up 20% from a year ago. Roles are full-time, part-time and seasonal, with seasonal pay averaging $20 per hour. Seasonal workers at 30 or more hours a week will get healthcare coverage from their first day starting Jan. 1, 2027.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service. Amazon is adding seasonal staff, with job postings each week from October through December.
why: Amazon captures almost 40 cents of every online dollar, per EMarketer, and Adobe projects $275.1 billion in online sales in November and December.

title: Mamdani says Amazon seeks to scare New Yorkers over delivery bill
sum: Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Amazon and other opponents of spending heavily to scare New Yorkers about the Delivery Protection Act, PoliticsNY reported. He is preparing to join national labor leaders in a push for the bill, which would require certain last-mile facilities to obtain city licenses and directly employ workers rather than use third-party contractors.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. The bill is still pending, and it would require certain last-mile facilities to hold city licenses and directly employ delivery workers if passed.
why: The bill would end third-party contractor use at licensed last-mile facilities in New York City, which could reshape how parcel carriers staff local delivery.
new: Mamdani publicly accused Amazon and other opponents of heavy spending to frighten New Yorkers and said he will join national labor leaders in the push; the earlier coverage did not include the mayor's own remarks, and there is no change yet for shippers.

title: USPS moves light Ground Advantage parcels to Hawaii by ship
sum: Effective Oct. 1, USPS extended Ground Advantage delivery expectations to 10 days or more for noncontiguous destinations including Hawaii, Alaska and Puerto Rico, according to Pacific Daily News. Packages under one pound now move primarily by surface transportation, and USPS spokesman John Hyatt said prices are unchanged. A Hawaii jewelry business owner told Pacific Business News that a dozen orders were still undelivered weeks after shipping.
plain: Since Oct. 1, Ground Advantage parcels to and from noncontiguous destinations are expected to take 10 days or more, with packages under one pound moving mainly by surface. USPS says prices are unchanged; Priority Mail is listed at 2 to 4 business days for Hawaii, Alaska, Puerto Rico, American Samoa and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and 2 to 6 for Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the Freely Associated States.
why: Ground Advantage shippers sending to Hawaii, Alaska, Puerto Rico and U.S. territories now face standard delivery windows of 10 days or more.
tie: USPS first extended delivery estimates for packages to and from Guam, Hawaii and other non-mainland locations on Oct. 1, 2026, with Hyatt saying prices were unchanged.

new: New detail is the operational cause: Ground Advantage parcels under one pound now move primarily by surface, with USPS citing hazardous materials risk on passenger aircraft, plus Priority Mail windows of 2 to 6 business days and a Dec. 16 holiday deadline that USPS kept in place, according to The Conveyor.

title: GLS US expands parcel delivery service into El Paso, Texas
sum: GLS US said on Oct. 20, 2026 that it is expanding parcel delivery into El Paso, extending its Texas network. The company said the move follows launches in Houston, Austin and San Antonio in 2026 and Dallas-Fort Worth in 2025.
plain: Businesses in El Paso can now ship with GLS US, which offers parcel delivery up to 150 pounds and international options. The release gives no rates or changes to existing customers' pricing.
why: El Paso adds a regional carrier option in West Texas; GLS US cites parcels up to 150 pounds and international shipping, with no pricing given.

title: Business groups urge NYC Council to block Delivery Protection Act
sum: A coalition including the Taxpayers Protection Alliance and the American Consumer Institute sent a letter to the City Council and Speaker Julie Menin on Tuesday opposing the Delivery Protection Act, the New York Post reported. The bill would bar delivery companies from using third-party contractors or gig workers in fulfillment and set a $500,000 penalty per non-employee worker. The bill has 35 co-sponsors and is laid over in committee, with no vote scheduled.
plain: No change to rates or service at present; the bill remains in committee with no vote scheduled.
why: The bill would bar contracted or gig delivery labor in New York City fulfillment operations, which the letter says would affect Amazon and UPS.
tie: Amazon had warned in October 2026 that it could close warehouses and move delivery jobs out of New York City if the bill passes.
new: Business groups sent a letter opposing the bill, and the co-sponsor count is now 35 versus 33 in earlier coverage; shippers see no direct change while the bill awaits a committee vote.

title: Amazon Prime Air plans Tallahassee drone deliveries by mid-November
sum: Amazon Prime Air is slated to start drone deliveries in Tallahassee, Florida, by mid-November, Josh Brundage of Prime Air said at a public showing of the MK30 drone on Oct. 20. Drones will carry items up to 5 pounds from the Mahan Drive fulfillment center to homes within 7.5 miles, and Brundage put the fee at $4.99. The structure that will house the drones is still under permit review, the Tallahassee Democrat reported.
plain: From mid-November, customers within 7.5 miles of Amazon's Mahan Drive site in Tallahassee could get drone delivery of items up to 5 pounds, with the fee given as $4.99. Brundage said cost varies by market and can be free, and the permit for the drone structure is still pending.
why: Shows the range, weight limit and fee for Amazon's drone delivery in a new Florida market, with up to 21 drones planned for the Tallahassee fleet.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026, with fees of $2.99 for Prime members and $4.99 for others.
new: Amazon gave a mid-November start for Tallahassee, with a $4.99 fee, 5-pound limit and 7.5-mile range, while its drone structure permit is pending; this is a local launch and does not change shipper rates elsewhere.

title: Coco, Serve Robotics face Illinois biometric suits over delivery robots
sum: Two class-action lawsuits filed in Cook County, Illinois, allege that delivery robots from Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics scan faces and hands and share the data with AI companies without consent. Both companies deny collecting biometric data. The suits cite the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, which carries fines of $1,000 to $5,000 per violation.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The suits are unresolved, and Chicago's robot delivery pilot is set to end in May 2027 unless officials extend it, according to TechEDT.
why: Sidewalk robots deliver DoorDash and Uber Eats orders in Chicago, and the suits seek to apply Illinois biometric law to them.
tie: The suits were first reported in October 2026, when ABC7 Chicago said Coco and Serve denied collecting biometric data or identifying individuals.
new: The article adds plaintiff details (a September 2025 DoorDash order, three Uber Eats deliveries), the allegation that data went to OpenAI and others, the $1,000-$5,000 per-violation fines and the May 2027 end of Chicago's pilot; shippers see no change to service.
syn: Two class-action lawsuits in Cook County, Illinois, claim that autonomous delivery robots from Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics collected facial features and hand shapes without written notice or permission, and shared the data with AI companies. One plaintiff says he ordered groceries through DoorDash in September 2025 and a Coco robot arrived. Another says he received three Uber Eats deliveries by Serve robot. Coco called the suit "frivolous" and Serve said its systems are not designed to identify individuals. The Illinois privacy law allows fines of $1,000 to $5,000 per violation.

aff.what: Sued over claims its robots captured faces, hands and body shape via cameras and LiDAR; it says it collected no biometric data in Chicago.
Sued over claims it collected video and sensor data and licensed it to third parties; it says the data is not used to identify people.
Set to end in May 2027 unless officials extend it, according to TechEDT.

title: EU to apply €2 per-line handling fee on non-EU shipments from 1 Nov
sum: The EU's €2 handling fee applies per line to distance-sales shipments arriving from outside the Union from 1 November, Air Cargo Week reported on 20 October. Product Identifier (PID) data is requested on all shipments from 26 October. The fee follows the €3 charge on low-value goods that began on 1 July.
plain: From 1 November, distance-sales shipments entering the EU from outside the Union face a €2 handling fee for each line, not just each parcel. PID data is requested on all shipments from 26 October.
why: The fee covers all distance sales into the EU and is charged per line, after small-parcel imports fell 30 to 40 percent in the two months following the July change, per the French Ministry of Economy.

title: Narvar names founder Amit Sharma CEO again
sum: Post-purchase platform Narvar said founder Amit Sharma is returning as CEO. Sharma moved to an advisory role in 2024, when Anisa Kumar took over as CEO. Narvar did not respond to a request for comment on Kumar's future role.
plain: No change to rates or service. The item concerns a leadership change at a post-purchase software provider.
why: Narvar says it works with more than 1,500 brands and retailers, which use its post-purchase tools for tracking and returns.

title: Amazon's Larsen says logistics network opened after seller demand
sum: Amazon Vice President Peter Larsen told Supply Chain 24/7 at the Gartner Supply Chain Symposium/Xpo in Orlando that Amazon opened its supply chain and logistics network to all businesses, including those that do not sell on Amazon. He said sellers had asked to use it for off-Amazon volume, and that Amazon had to detach services from its seller ID requirement.
plain: Businesses that do not sell on Amazon can now use its supply chain and logistics network, according to Amazon. The interview gives no prices, rates or effective dates.
why: Amazon's network, previously tied to its own sellers, is now open to any business, widening the carrier options available to shippers outside Amazon.
new: Amazon's Peter Larsen explained in an interview that seller requests for off-Amazon volume and the removal of seller ID dependencies led to opening the network, and said bulk distribution capability was only added this year.

title: UPS, Teamsters agree nationwide Driver Choice buyout, capped at 7,500
sum: UPS said it reached an agreement with the Teamsters to offer its voluntary Driver Choice Program nationwide, including the Central Region. The Teamsters said eligible drivers who accept get $150,000 payments for early retirement, with total severance payments capped at 7,500 drivers.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. UPS said applications will be approved based on seniority and business needs.
why: UPS is reconfiguring its network, and the Teamsters said up to 7,500 drivers across national job classifications could take buyouts under the agreement.
tie: UPS withdrew the program in the Teamsters' Central Region in March 2026 after local unions filed grievances, and an earlier April 2026 report described a settlement capping it at 7,500 drivers.
new: UPS and the Teamsters detailed the terms: $150,000 early-retirement payments, offers by seniority to long-haul feeder and Regular Package Drivers, and the Central Region included; the sources report no change to shipper rates or service.

title: Royal Mail disputes CWU leadership claims, cites 85% First Class on-time rate
sum: Royal Mail said recent statements by CWU leadership do not reflect the state of the business or its Christmas preparations. It said it is hiring an additional 22,000 seasonal workers, with over 100,000 applications received, and that 85% of First Class letters were delivered on time in the latest reporting period, up from 76% a year earlier.
plain: No change to rates or service was announced. Royal Mail said it is preparing for Christmas peak with 22,000 additional seasonal workers.
why: Royal Mail's statement on peak staffing and letter delivery rates comes as it rolls out Universal Service reform in around 90% of delivery offices.

title: ShipStation Global details 250+ AI agents running across its platform
sum: ShipStation Global said it runs more than 250 AI agents and automation bots in production and is on pace for over 5 million agentic actions in 2026. The company, which connects to more than 350 parcel carriers, reported figures on customer support, label pre-filling and freight tracking.
plain: No change to rates or service. ShipStation Global said its AI features cover label pre-filling, support and freight quoting for its customers.
why: ShipStation Global connects to more than 350 parcel carriers, so its AI tooling reaches small and mid-sized shippers using its software.

title: MAK Acquisition terminates UniUni purchase agreement
sum: MAK Acquisition Corp. said on Oct. 20, 2026 that it delivered a notice of termination to Uni Express Inc. (UniUni) under the purchase agreement dated May 15, 2026. MAK said the proposed reverse take-over will not proceed and that it is withdrawing its preliminary prospectus dated June 10, 2026.
plain: No change to rates or service. The proposed transaction between MAK and UniUni will not proceed, according to MAK.
why: The termination ends a planned reverse take-over that would have taken UniUni, a parcel delivery company, public through a TSX-listed SPAC.

title: USPS issues interim rule on customs charges for international mailers
sum: The Postal Service published an interim final rule revising the International Mail Manual to update mailer responsibilities on customs requirements. It also sets procedures for paying or reimbursing customs charges assessed on a mailpiece, including after postage is bought. The rule took effect October 19, 2026, and comments are due November 18, 2026.
plain: From October 19, 2026, mailers must use a delivered duty paid basis where the destination country requires it. The Postal Service may invoice mailers for duties, taxes, import fees and other charges not paid in full through USPS Delivered Duty Paid service.
why: International mailers sending to the EU may be invoiced for duties, taxes and import fees that postage does not cover, according to the Postal Service.
new: The Postal Service now says it may invoice mailers for duties, taxes and import fees not paid in full via its Delivered Duty Paid service, following the European Commission's removal of the de minimis exemption for most low-value goods on July 1, 2026.

title: DoorDash adds Macy's to retail marketplace, plans November returns rollout
sum: A TIKR stock analysis says DoorDash added Macy's, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland to its retail marketplace. DoorDash will handle pickup and returns of app purchases for a flat $7.99 fee, with a nationwide rollout planned for November. TIKR cites Q2 revenue up 36% to $4.5 billion and marketplace gross order value up 36% to $33.1 billion.
plain: DoorDash plans a nationwide rollout in November of pickup and returns for retail app purchases at a flat $7.99 fee. The source reports no change to carrier rates or surcharges.
why: DoorDash's retail push adds a $7.99 pickup-and-returns service, with a nationwide rollout planned for November, according to TIKR's analysis.

title: Maersk adds North American delivery services to Shipstore platform
sum: A.P. Moller – Maersk has partnered with Shipstore so its North American e-commerce delivery services can be accessed directly in Shipstore's shipping automation platform, according to LM - Logistics Manager. Maersk currently handles more than 10 million e-commerce parcels annually across North America.
plain: Shippers with a Maersk delivery programme can manage Maersk delivery alongside other carriers inside Shipstore. No change to rates or fees was reported.
why: Shipstore users with a Maersk delivery programme get another carrier option in one system; Maersk handles over 10 million North American e-commerce parcels a year.

title: Massachusetts lawmakers ask Healey to freeze drone delivery permits
sum: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators asked Gov. Maura Healey, Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll and Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell in an Oct. 19 letter to create a drone delivery task force. They also asked that state agencies stop accepting or processing certificate applications from drone delivery operators until its review is done. Healey's office said it is "evaluating our options," according to a State House News Service report the Boston Globe ran on Oct. 21. The letter responds to Amazon's plan to fly Prime Air drones from its Westborough warehouse.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon's Westborough drone deliveries have not started, and the request, if adopted, could affect when and where drone hubs get state approval.
why: The request targets state approval of drone landing sites; Amazon's Westborough hub could reach 15 cities and towns named in the letter.
tie: The letter follows Amazon's August 2026 announcement that Prime Air would expand drone deliveries to almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.
new: Sixteen Massachusetts legislators now ask for a state freeze on drone delivery certificate applications and a task force; no fees or service terms change, but the timing of Amazon's Westborough launch remains uncertain.

title: USPS finalizes live animal mailing rules in Publication 52
sum: The Postal Service published a final rule revising Publication 52 to improve package integrity and container identification for live animal shipments, effective October 19, 2026. It follows an August 6, 2026 proposal (91 FR 50741), and USPS said it received 32 formal responses.
plain: Mailers shipping live animals through USPS must individually address and number each container in multi-container shipments bound together. Reuse of fiberboard containers is prohibited for all live animal shipments, effective October 19, 2026.
why: The rule changes packaging and labeling requirements for mailers sending live animals, including multi-container shipments and adult birds.

title: UPS opens $80m+ Clark hub in the Philippines, 15 times its predecessor's size
sum: UPS opened a new hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines, developed from an investment of more than US$80m, according to Supply Chain Digital Magazine. The hub covers 30,000 square meters, is set to process an average of 46,000 packages a day and has capacity for 15,000 packages an hour.
plain: No change to rates or fees. UPS said service to and from eastern China and other major Asia Pacific markets will be up to two days faster, and Southeast Asia-India service up to two days faster.
why: The hub adds capacity across more than 1,100 trade lanes and, UPS said, cuts transit by up to two days between eastern China, Southeast Asia and India.

title: Westborough, Mass., voters ban commercial drone pads in 510-13 vote
sum: Westborough, Massachusetts, voters passed a general bylaw on October 19 banning any commercial drone launch pad, landing pad or delivery drop zone in town, by 510 to 13 at a Special Town Meeting, DroneXL reported. The measure was written in response to Amazon's plan to fly Prime Air MK30 drones from its warehouse at 64 Otis Street. It sets a $300 fine per offense and takes effect after the state attorney general approves it or 90 days pass without action.
plain: No change to shipper rates or service. The bylaw bans commercial drone pads and drop zones in Westborough and takes effect only after attorney general approval or 90 days without action.
why: Amazon's Westborough drone hub now faces a town ban, a zoning appeal, a planning hearing and a congressional letter deadline.
tie: Amazon presented its pad plan to the Select Board on August 18 and told residents in September it hoped to be flying by late October, according to the article.
new: Westborough voters approved a bylaw on October 19 banning commercial drone pads and drop zones, adding a local hurdle to one Amazon site; the attorney general's review is pending, so nothing changes yet for shippers.

title: USPS files two new competitive shipping contracts with PRC
sum: The Postal Regulatory Commission noticed two USPS filings on negotiated service agreements, both accepted October 19, 2026. One adds Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail & USPS Ground Advantage Contract 1514 to the Competitive product list, with comments due October 27, 2026. The other adds a fulfillment product, PM-GA Contract 1114, under summary review.
plain: The notice does not change published rates or service for shippers. It covers two negotiated contracts, with the pricing and customer details filed under seal.
why: The filings show USPS adding negotiated competitive contracts for Priority Mail, Ground Advantage and fulfillment, though the notice withholds the customers and the terms.
tie: Earlier coverage reported a new USPS agreement with Amazon in April 2026 and an exclusive DHL eCommerce last-mile deal in May 2026, but this notice does not name the counterparties to either contract.
new: The PRC notice shows USPS filing Contract 1514 (Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail & USPS Ground Advantage) and fulfillment product PM-GA Contract 1114, with no named customers, so nothing here changes rates or service for shippers.

title: Police: $963,000 in trading cards stolen from FedEx truck in Southern California
sum: Santa Ana police said on Oct. 19 that thieves took an estimated $963,000 in trading cards from a FedEx truck, with shipments from Professional Sports Authenticator, and that the valuation could rise. No arrests or recoveries had been announced. Verisk CargoNet estimated Q2 2026 cargo theft losses at $304.6 million across the U.S. and Canada, against $135.7 million a year earlier.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report concerns a theft from a FedEx truck and industry cargo theft statistics.
why: CargoNet put Q2 2026 U.S. and Canada cargo theft losses at $304.6 million even as incidents fell, with costly thefts driving the total.

title: Amazon warns it could pull NYC delivery jobs over Delivery Protection Act
sum: Amazon has warned it could shut warehouses and move roughly 5,000 delivery jobs out of New York City if the Delivery Protection Act passes, The Times of India reported. The bill, backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, would require Amazon to directly employ drivers who now work for third-party contractors. Analysts cited in the report said the company could close all 15 of its last-mile stations in the city, affecting 2,000 warehouse workers.
plain: No change to rates or service yet, as the bill has not passed. If it passes and Amazon follows through, delivery operations in New York City could be relocated or closed, according to analysts cited in the report.
why: The bill would affect about 5,000 Amazon drivers and 40 delivery service partners in New York City, and analysts say Amazon could close all 15 last-mile stations there.
new: Analysts now say Amazon could pull 5,000 contracted driver roles and close all 15 city last-mile stations, citing its Montreal closures, which for shippers points to possible delivery changes in New York City only if the bill passes.

title: Shipt adds more than 500 Sprouts locations to its marketplace
sum: Shipt added more than 500 Sprouts Farmers Market locations to its marketplace, widening same-day delivery access to the grocer, according to a Simply Wall Street article. The article is investor commentary and gives no launch date or terms.
plain: Shoppers can order from more Sprouts stores through Shipt's same-day delivery marketplace. The article gives no change to carrier rates, fees or parcel service.

title: PSA says graded cards stolen from FedEx truck; collector reports $100,000+ loss
sum: PSA said it is aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items and is working with law enforcement and the carrier. A collector named SKY-B said on Oct. 17 that PSA told him a FedEx truck carrying his 104-card order was burglarized after leaving its Southern California location, with more than $100,000 of cards taken.
plain: No change to FedEx rates or service. PSA said it is arranging compensation for affected customers based on fair market value, up to the Maximum Insured Value selected for each item.
why: Reported theft of graded cards in FedEx transit, with one dealer's estimate of $500K declared value, raises questions about insured-value claims on high-value shipments.

title: Amazon warns it may close 15 New York City warehouses over delivery bill
sum: Amazon has warned it may close 15 distribution warehouses in New York City, affecting about 7,000 jobs, if the Delivery Protection Act passes as written, Vietnam.vn reported. The bill would require Amazon to directly hire more than 5,000 delivery workers now employed through independent contractors. No voting date has been set.
plain: No change yet; the bill has no vote date. Amazon says that if its New York warehouses close, some same-day orders could move to next-day delivery and fewer items could qualify for expedited Prime delivery.
why: About 5,000 delivery workers at roughly 40 contractor firms and 2,000 warehouse staff are in scope, and Amazon says same-day and Prime speeds could change.

title: FedEx vehicle carrying PSA card orders is burglarized in Southern California
sum: PSA emailed customers that after leaving its Southern California facility, a FedEx vehicle transporting PSA orders was burglarized, according to screenshots card creator SKY-B shared on X on Oct. 17. Resell Calendar reported one collector valued a stolen 104-card submission at over $100,000, and said total losses may top $1 million, which is its own estimate. A list compiled by Boston Card Hunter from user reports mentioned 383 cards.
plain: No change to FedEx rates or service has been announced. PSA told affected customers it will compensate based on fair market value up to each item's Maximum Insured Value, with more details to follow.
why: PSA customers' graded orders were stolen in transit; a user-compiled list cites 383 cards, and PSA says compensation details are due.

title: Amazon passes 1 million robots in its facilities, Futurism reports
sum: Futurism reported that Amazon has surpassed a fleet of 1 million robots, including mechanical arms, floor loaders and pallet sorting machines. It cited an Ars Technica interview with George Mason University business professor Brad Greenwood, who said the robots are physically close to workers and can dictate the pace of work. Joan Moriarty of the Strategic Organizing Center told Ars that Amazon's workplace injuries are a topic the company avoids.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report concerns Amazon's internal warehouse automation and its workforce.
why: Futurism says the robots help speed up delivery times at a company with over 1.5 million full- and part-time workers.

title: Ceva merges Colis Privé into Paack, unifies last-mile brand
sum: Ceva Logistics said on Friday it has merged its France-focused last-mile unit Colis Privé into Paack, which it acquired in early August. The unified Paack brand will roll out progressively to customers and partners from January, Ceva said. The combined business delivers 150 million parcels annually through a network of 17,000 out-of-home delivery points.
plain: Retailers using Colis Privé or Paack will see the networks combined under a single Paack brand, rolled out progressively from January. The sources state no rate or service changes.
why: The merged unit handles 150 million parcels a year across France, Spain, Portugal, Belgium and Luxembourg, which Ceva said will simplify delivery for multi-market e-commerce retailers.
tie: Ceva acquired Paack in early August, and when the tentative deal was first announced last summer the expectation was that Colis Privé would absorb Paack, according to FreightWaves.

title: Ofcom proposes extending Royal Mail Second Class stamp cap to March 2028
sum: Ofcom proposed extending its inflation-pegged safeguard cap on Royal Mail Second Class stamp prices by one year, to March 2028. The current cap, set in 2024, expires in March 2027. Ofcom said it plans to consult on its long-term approach to pricing next year, and its Policy Director Fergal Farragher called Royal Mail's financial position "stark".
plain: Under the proposal, the Second Class stamp price would stay flat in real terms until March 2028 rather than the cap lapsing in March 2027. It is a proposal and not yet a final decision.
why: The proposal would keep Royal Mail's Second Class stamp price flat in real terms to March 2028, with a longer-term pricing review planned for 2027.

dates.w: Current Royal Mail Second Class price cap expires (month stated)

title: Westborough drafts rules for FAA on Amazon Prime Air drone deliveries
sum: The town of Westborough, Massachusetts, drafted rules it wants the FAA to enforce on Amazon's drone delivery plans during a Thursday meeting, Boston 25 News reported. Some residents raised privacy and noise concerns. Amazon plans to deliver packages under 5 pounds within a 7.5-mile radius of its fulfillment center, and lawmakers requested a response by the end of October.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. Amazon's proposed Prime Air service in Westborough remains a plan, and the town's rules are a request to the FAA.
why: Local pushback and a congressional request could bear on where Amazon's Prime Air drone delivery, limited to packages under 5 pounds, can operate.
tie: Amazon held a community meeting in Westborough in September to discuss its proposed Prime Air drone delivery service, according to the report.

title: Mfume requests USPS briefing on suspicious mailings to Congress
sum: Rep. Kweisi Mfume (D-MD), ranking member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations, wrote to Postmaster General David Steiner and Chief Postal Inspector Gary Barksdale asking for a briefing on suspicious mailings sent this week to congressional offices and state election offices. Mfume said state election officials and a Senate office reported that postal employees intercepted several of the letters before delivery.
plain: No change to rates or service.
why: The request concerns security of mail handled by USPS employees and the Postal Inspection Service, and asks whether the Inspection Service needs more resources.

title: Oregon lawmakers press USPS on mail delivery problems on state's north coast
sum: Rep. Suzanne Bonamici and Sens. Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley sent a letter to Postmaster General Steiner on Oct. 16, 2026, about delivery problems in Astoria, Warrenton, Gearhart and Rainier. They asked for a written response within 14 days and an informational session for residents within 60 days.
plain: No change to USPS rates or service has been announced. The lawmakers say some Astoria businesses and local governments get mail irregularly or not at all, and some Gearhart and Rainier residents lack home delivery.

title: Two Cook County suits accuse Coco, Serve robots of biometric scans
sum: Two lawsuits filed in Cook County allege that sidewalk delivery robots run by Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics scan the faces, hands and bodies of customers and passersby in Chicago without consent, according to ABC7 Chicago. Coco said it has not collected biometric data in Chicago, and Serve said it will defend against the complaint and that its systems are not designed to identify individuals.
plain: No change to rates or service. The suits are pending, and the city's robot pilot is set to expire in May 2027 unless extended, according to CBS Chicago.
tie: Serve Robotics entered Chicago in September 2025 through an Uber Eats partnership, according to the sources.

title: DHL Group raises 2026 EBIT outlook to above 7.0 billion euros
sum: DHL Group raised its full-year 2026 outlook on Oct. 16, saying reported Group EBIT should exceed 7.0 billion euros, up from more than 6.5 billion euros. In an ad hoc disclosure, it cited earnings momentum at Express and signs of a robust Q4 peak. Preliminary Q3 Group EBIT was around 1.71 billion euros on revenue of around 22.6 billion euros.
plain: No change to rates or service. The announcement covers DHL Group's earnings and cash-flow outlook.

title: Amazon and Teamsters file Fifth Circuit briefs over JFK8 bargaining order
sum: Amazon and the Teamsters-aligned ALU-IBT Local 1 filed briefs on October 16 in the Fifth Circuit over an April NLRB order requiring Amazon to bargain at its JFK8 warehouse in Staten Island, FreeightWaves reported. Amazon says it has not bargained because it is seeking court review of the union certification.
plain: No change to rates or service. The case concerns whether Amazon must bargain with the union at its JFK8 warehouse in Staten Island.
why: The case decides whether Amazon must bargain with a union at JFK8, its only warehouse where a union election win has been certified, according to the article.
syn: Amazon and ALU-International Brotherhood of Teamsters Local 1 filed briefs on October 16 in the Fifth Circuit in Amazon's challenge to an April National Labor Relations Board order to bargain with the union at JFK8 in Staten Island, FreightWaves reported. Amazon said it has not bargained because an employer cannot directly appeal a union certification and must refuse to bargain to obtain court review. The union's 115-page brief reviews the full history of the dispute, while Amazon's brief rests on narrower legal grounds. The article describes a separate NLRB matter over whether Amazon is a joint employer of delivery service providers as still pending.

aff.what: The Fifth Circuit will review the NLRB's April order requiring Amazon to bargain with ALU-IBT Local 1.
A separate NLRB joint-employer dispute continues over an April agreement between Amazon and the NLRB General Counsel.

title: Bronx Amazon DSP operators oppose NYC Delivery Protection Act
sum: Delivery service provider operators in the Bronx are speaking out against the Delivery Protection Act, which the Bronx Times said would effectively eliminate delivery contractors in New York City. The bill has supermajority council support but has not been called for a vote, and Amazon has said it would consider relocating its warehouses outside the city.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. The bill, which has not been scheduled for a vote, would end subcontracted delivery arrangements and create a licensing system and safety standards for distribution facilities in New York City.
new: The Bronx Times reported DSP operators' opposition, Amazon's statement that it would consider relocating warehouses outside the city, and that over 40 DSPs employing over 5,000 workers operate in New York City; there is still no vote date and no change for shippers.

title: UPS Capital launches CommerceShield AI delivery risk score for retailers
sum: UPS Capital, the financial services arm of UPS, recently launched CommerceShield, which runs large language models on two years of UPS shipping data to predict whether a delivery will succeed. UPS Capital said the data covers more than 26 billion delivery touchpoints across more than 150 million U.S. addresses. The score is combined with other signals, such as device and email data, to give retailers a combined risk score.
plain: Retailers using CommerceShield can see a predicted delivery-success score and attach actions such as requiring a signature or routing a delivery to a staffed pickup point. No change to UPS rates or service levels was announced.
why: The tool gives retailers a delivery-risk score from UPS data, and UPS Capital survey data cited in the article shows consumers often blame retailers for lost packages.

title: UPS launches Secure Commerce suite for shipping fraud and loss protection
sum: UPS has launched UPS Secure Commerce, a suite of tools meant to help businesses prevent shipping fraud, reduce losses and manage supply chain disruptions, The Atlanta 100 reported. It combines InsureShield insurance, Parcel Pro protection for high-value shipments and CommerceShield risk-identification technology. UPS said it insured 62 million packages for 1.4 million shippers in 2025 and resolved 97% of claims within five days.
plain: UPS now offers InsureShield, Parcel Pro and CommerceShield together as UPS Secure Commerce. The article gives no pricing and no change to shipping rates or fees.

It includes zone definitions, billable weight rules and a List Rates table by weight (1 lb up to at least 43 lbs in the text provided) and zone (2-8).
