title: FedEx retirees' pension class action advances in district court
sum: A district court judge, Thomas L. Parker, on Thursday allowed FedEx retirees' proposed class action over how their pensions are calculated to move forward, Bloomberg Law reported. The retirees allege FedEx used unreasonable calculation methods. The Sixth Circuit had earlier revived the case.
plain: No change to rates or service. The ruling concerns a pension dispute between FedEx and its retirees.

title: Richardson, Texas, residents cite Amazon Prime Air drone noise
sum: Residents of Richardson, Texas, a Dallas suburb where Amazon has tested Prime Air drone deliveries throughout 2026, told The New York Times the drones are loud and can fly as low as 150 feet over homes, according to Mashable. An Amazon spokesperson said "fewer than 1 percent" of complaints this year concerned noise. One resident counted 52 drones over her house on a single Friday.
plain: No change to Amazon delivery fees or service terms was reported. The story covers resident complaints in Richardson, Texas, where Amazon has been testing drone deliveries.
why: Local noise and privacy complaints in a test market surface as Prime Air expands toward nearly 500 towns and cities, according to Mashable.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026, up from 11 U.S. locations.
new: Residents of Amazon's Richardson, Texas test community have complained about noise and privacy, per the NYT as reported by Mashable; Amazon said noise is under 1 percent of complaints, with no stated change to fees or service for shippers.

title: USPS says it is ready for midterm ballots; extra measures start October 24
sum: Postmaster General David Steiner told reporters the Postal Service is "absolutely ready" to handle ballots for the November 3 midterm elections. USPS said its extraordinary measures begin October 24 and include extended hours at some retail locations, expedited handling, extra deliveries and special pickups of ballots. In 2024, USPS delivered 99.2 million ballots to and from voters.
plain: From October 24, USPS says it will expedite completed ballots to election offices, including local turnaround that bypasses processing when needed. The sources state no change to rates or fees. USPS advised voters to mail ballots at least a week before they are due.
tie: The Supreme Court declined on Sept. 14 to let USPS enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, and USPS said it would not enforce the rule under the order.

title: Kirkwood council kills Walmart-Wing drone delivery proposal
sum: The Kirkwood, Missouri, City Council let a proposal for Walmart drone deliveries die on Thursday after members declined to vote on it, the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported. Walmart and Wing had asked the city to approve a drone launchpad in the parking lot of the Kirkwood Walmart. Residents opposed the plan at the council meeting.
plain: Walmart and Wing cannot build the proposed drone launchpad at the Kirkwood Walmart under this proposal. Nothing changes for shippers' rates or service.

title: Zipline starts drone delivery for Teriyaki Madness in Texas
sum: Teriyaki Madness said that beginning Oct. 15 it is partnering with Zipline to deliver orders by autonomous drone across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and Houston later this year, starting at its Denton location. Orders are placed in the Zipline app, and the companies said most arrive in less than five minutes. Zipline said it has flown more than 140 million autonomous miles since 2014.
plain: From Oct. 15, customers of Teriyaki Madness's Denton location can get drone delivery by ordering through the Zipline app, with more Texas shops to follow. No change to parcel carrier rates, fees or service.
new: Zipline adds restaurant brand Teriyaki Madness as a customer in Texas, starting in Denton; the announcement does not mention Part 108 and changes no parcel rates for shippers.

title: Serve Robotics, Cyan Robotics hit with Illinois biometric suits
sum: Two robotics companies face separate proposed class actions alleging their camera-equipped delivery robots scanned and stored consumers' facial and hand geometry without notice or consent, in violation of the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, Bloomberg Law reported. Serve Robotics has operated robots for Uber Eats and Grubhub in 14 Chicago-area neighborhoods since September 2025, according to a suit filed by lead plaintiff Barry Schain in Cook County Circuit Court. Cyan Robotics has operated robots for Uber Eats and DoorDash in Chicago neighborhoods since late 2024, according to a similar proposed class action.
plain: No change to rates or service is reported. The suits are allegations in proposed class actions and have not been decided.

title: UPS opens $80M international air hub at Clark airport in the Philippines
sum: UPS opened its International Air Hub at Clark International Airport in Pampanga on 15 October 2026, with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. attending the grand opening, according to the Daily Tribune. The US$80 million, 30,000-square-meter facility can process up to 15,000 packages per hour and is expected to support 170 weekly flight segments.
plain: No change to UPS rates or fees was announced. The hub is expected to cut transit times by up to two days on selected routes serving Eastern China, Southeast Asia and India, with some shipments arriving in as little as one business day.

title: FBI, USPS inspectors probe suspicious mailings to election officials
sum: The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service said on Thursday (Oct 15) they are investigating suspicious mailings sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterms, according to Reuters. The FBI said some letters contained an unknown substance, and some were intercepted before delivery.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. USPS said earlier this month it would take extraordinary measures for the 2026 election, including extended retail hours and special ballot pickups.

title: USPS files notice to add shipping services contract to NSA list
sum: The Postal Service gave notice in the Federal Register on Oct. 15, 2026 that it filed a request with the Postal Regulatory Commission. The request would add a domestic shipping services contract to the Negotiated Service Agreements in the Mail Classification Schedule's Competitive Products List. The notice, filed under Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage categories, names no customer or rates in the text provided.
plain: No change to published USPS rates or service for shippers generally.
why: Negotiated agreements set contract terms for individual customers outside published rates, so this filing affects the contracting customer rather than shippers generally.
new: USPS filed a request on Oct. 15, 2026 to add a domestic shipping services contract to its negotiated agreements list; the notice does not name the customer, so it is not stated to relate to Amazon or DHL eCommerce, and it changes nothing for shippers generally.

title: Veho appoints Henrik Nilsmo as chief revenue officer
sum: Veho announced on Oct. 15, 2026 that Henrik Nilsmo has been appointed Chief Revenue Officer, leading its commercial organization. According to the announcement, Nilsmo previously served as CRO at EBANX and spent six years at Klarna, and brings 14 years of experience building commercial organizations at technology companies.
plain: No change to rates or service. The appointment affects Veho's internal commercial leadership.

title: Opinion: Labor, trade and security policy reshape parcel competition
sum: In an opinion piece for FreightWaves, Daniil Davydoff of DHL eCommerce Americas argues that labor rules, geopolitics and data security may shape which parcel carriers succeed as much as operations do. He cites a $131.5 million settlement by DoorDash and Uber with New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection. He also cites an industry analysis showing UPS and FedEx fuel surcharges above 23%, up from about 9% in 2021, and a SpeedX incident that exposed 840 million customer records.
plain: No change to rates or service. The piece is one author's view of policy pressures on carriers, and it says fuel surcharges for UPS and FedEx are above 23% according to an industry analysis.

title: Amazon Prime Air to expand drone delivery to nearly 500 US cities by end of 2026
sum: Amazon said Prime Air will expand to nearly 500 cities and towns in the US by the end of 2026, about six times its current footprint of 11 sites in 10 metro areas, according to Mashable. The next launches are planned for the Chicago, Syracuse, Cleveland, Atlanta and Boise metro areas. Amazon has not yet published a full list of the places included.
plain: Customers at eligible addresses will see drone delivery as an option at checkout, for most items of 5 pounds or less. Prime members pay nothing on orders of $50 or more and $2.99 on smaller orders, and non-Prime customers pay $4.99, according to Amazon.
why: Prime Air's planned reach is about six times its current footprint, with drone delivery offered at checkout for eligible items of 5 pounds or less.
tie: Amazon outlined the same Prime Air expansion to nearly 500 towns in August 2026, including the $2.99 and $4.99 delivery fees.
new: Mashable reports that Amazon counts cities and towns rather than launch sites, with each site covering roughly 175 square miles, and that Boise is among the next metro areas; no full list of places is published yet, so which shippers' customers qualify remains unclear.

title: Amazon seeks permit for Prime Air drone center in Portland
sum: Amazon is working with local officials on Prime Air drone delivery in Portland, spokesperson Farah Jad told The Oregonian/OregonLive, without giving a launch or flight-testing date. Permitting records first reported by The Portland Business Journal show Amazon seeking a pre-application conference for a Prime Air Drone Delivery Center at its same-day fulfillment site at 515 N. Schmeer Road.
plain: No change to rates or service yet; Portland has no announced drone delivery start date. Amazon's stated drone fees are free for Prime members on orders over $50 and $2.99 below that, and $4.99 for non-members.
tie: Amazon said in an August 2026 news release that Prime Air was in 11 cities and planned to expand to nearly 500 by the end of the year, with Portland on the list.
new: Portland is confirmed as a Prime Air target, with Amazon seeking a pre-application conference for a drone delivery center at an existing Portland-area fulfillment site, but no launch date has been given, so no shipper pricing or service change takes effect yet.

title: CWU calls for emergency summit to address Royal Mail crisis
sum: The Communication Workers Union called for a summit of the government, employers and union representatives on Royal Mail, saying the company is "on the brink of collapse." General Secretary Dave Ward cited recruitment and retention problems, and the call followed BBC reporting of a "nightmare Christmas" for the company.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The union's call concerns staffing and the company's future, and the BBC has reported recruitment and retention problems ahead of Christmas.
why: Royal Mail staffing problems reported by the BBC and the union could affect delivery service over the Christmas period for businesses and consumers.

title: FedEx doubles Taoyuan airport hub in Taiwan to 19,000 square meters
sum: FedEx has expanded its cargo hub at Taoyuan International Airport, doubling it to 19,000 square meters, Radio Taiwan International reported. Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim attended the opening ceremony on a Wednesday. The automated sorting system handles 9,000 packages per hour.
plain: No change to rates or fees was announced. The report says the new automated system raises import efficiency 2.5 times and export efficiency 1.2 times at the Taoyuan hub.
why: The expansion adds automated import and export capacity at FedEx's Taiwan hub, which handles 9,000 packages per hour, according to Radio Taiwan International.

title: PRC notices three new USPS standardized competitive contracts
sum: The Postal Regulatory Commission published a notice of three Postal Service requests to add standardized distinct products to the Competitive product list. They are PM-GA Contract 1111 and Contract 1113 (Mid-Market) and Contract 1112 (Fulfillment), all accepted October 15, 2026.
plain: The notice does not state any change to published rates or service. It concerns individual negotiated agreements, with some materials filed under seal.
why: The filings add three negotiated Competitive contracts, which are reviewed in summary proceedings with no public comment period.

title: UPS, FedEx say holiday-season domestic volume is flat on soft demand
sum: UPS said its domestic volume in the first two weeks of the holiday peak season was flat compared with 1999, after growth slowed to 4% in October and November from 5.5% over the first nine months of the year. FedEx said softer volumes, which it tied to a slowing U.S. economy and severe weather, mean domestic growth at FedEx Express and FedEx Ground is expected to be flat or slightly down for the month.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service was announced. The carriers reported softer shipment volumes in the holiday season.

title: Teamsters, NYC-DSA canvass Speaker Menin's district for Amazon driver bill
sum: The Indypendent reports that Teamsters Local 804, Amazon drivers and the NYC-DSA Labor Working Group canvassed on Oct. 3 in Speaker Julie Menin's district to press for a vote on the Delivery Protection Act. The bill has 33 of 51 Councilmembers as cosponsors, but no action has been taken since an April committee hearing. Further canvassing is set for Oct. 17 and a City Hall rally for Oct. 22.
plain: No change to rates or service for now, since the bill has not come to a vote. Amazon-funded ads argue it would raise delivery costs for New Yorkers.
why: The bill would bar Amazon and others from using third-party delivery contractors in New York City, and 33 of the 51 Councilmembers have cosponsored it.
tie: Amazon's opposition to the bill, including testimony at the April hearing, was also covered in October 2026 reporting on Bronx delivery service provider operators.
new: The Indypendent reports that organizers have knocked on more than 11,000 doors, that Amazon gave $5 million to a group funding ads against the bill, and that canvassing and a rally are set for Oct. 17 and Oct. 22; nothing changes for shippers unless the bill passes.

title: WWEX Group and Auctane merge to form ShipStation Global
sum: WWEX Group and Auctane have completed a merger to form ShipStation Global, a shipping platform for small and mid-size shippers, Dealroom reported. Terms were not disclosed. The company has added less-than-truckload (LTL) freight booking to the ShipStation platform.
plain: No change to published rates or fees. ShipStation platform customers can now get LTL quotes and book pallet shipments, according to Dealroom, with no minimum volume commitments or existing carrier accounts required.

title: Manna adds three Tulsa drone bases, plans 1,000 US jobs
sum: Manna Air Delivery said on Oct. 14, 2026 that it is opening three more drone bases in Tulsa, Oklahoma, weeks after launching its first US site there. Each base can complete up to 24 deliveries per hour, and the company said it plans over 1,000 US manufacturing jobs over the next three years.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. Customers in Manna's initial Tulsa service areas can order meals, groceries and essentials through the Manna app.
why: A drone operator with almost 400,000 commercial flights is scaling a US network for food and essentials, adding to a field that includes Amazon, Wing and Walmart.
new: Manna said on Oct. 14 it is adding three Tulsa bases and planning sites in Oklahoma and Texas, which widens the set of US drone networks but does not change shipper rates or service.

title: Lawmakers ask FAA, Amazon for separate review of Westborough drone hub
sum: Sens. Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren and Reps. Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan asked Amazon and the FAA on Oct. 14 to put Prime Air's proposed Westborough, Massachusetts, drone hub through its own environmental assessment with a public comment period. Separate letters went to Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, and both ask for a written answer by Oct. 29.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon is hoping to start drone deliveries from the Westborough fulfillment center by the end of the year, and the lawmakers want a site-specific assessment first.
tie: In August 2026 Amazon said Prime Air would start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from new sites, and on Sept. 28 state lawmakers from the Westborough area asked the company to pause its plans there.
new: Federal lawmakers have joined state lawmakers in pressing for a separate FAA environmental assessment of the Westborough hub, which could bear on Amazon's hoped-for start of drone deliveries there by the end of 2026.

title: Lithuanian regulator approves DHL purchase of Venipak Baltic units
sum: Lithuania's competition authority said Wednesday it approved DHL eCommerce International Holdings' acquisition of Venipak Lietuva, Venipak Latvija and Venipak Eesti, according to an MLex summary. The companies provide parcel delivery and freight transport services. The full article was not available, so terms are not stated.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The source summary covers only the regulatory approval.

title: UPS parcel pivot draws split views as analysts weigh 2028 Teamsters talks
sum: A FreightWaves analysis reports that analysts and an industry consultant disagree on whether UPS's stated focus on premium and logistics services means it will leave parts of parcel delivery. Satish Jindel said UPS does not intend to exit any part of parcel, while UPS officials told the outlet privately that small package is not going away. UPS's Aug. 31 release described a new global operating model and named Matt Guffey chief U.S. domestic officer over all parcel and delivery units.
plain: No change to UPS rates or service is announced. The piece reflects analyst and consultant views on UPS's strategy and on the next Teamsters contract, which it places in 2028.
tie: UPS's Aug. 31 release described a new global operating model built around integrated logistics and put all parcel and delivery units under Matt Guffey, according to the article.
new: The piece adds specifics beyond the earlier coverage: UPS has cut 150 sort centers, 30,000 positions and 50 million labor hours and plans to invest over $8 billion over four years in automation. It also cites labor-cost comparisons of about $65 per hour for Teamsters drivers against $35 to $39 for FedEx drivers, and mixed views on a 2028 strike. No shipper rates or services change as a result.

title: GOFO launches Mailbox Parcel letterbox service in the Netherlands
sum: GOFO, a last-mile delivery carrier, said it is offering GOFO Mailbox Parcel in the Netherlands from October 14, 2026. The service covers parcels up to 38 × 26.5 × 3.2 cm and 2 kg, with next-working-day delivery, real-time tracking and photo proof of delivery. GOFO said a one-month pilot on its Dutch network reached a 98.5% next-working-day delivery rate.
plain: Shippers in the Netherlands with small, lightweight orders can use a new GOFO letterbox delivery option from October 14, 2026. No rates were stated, and nothing changes for existing GOFO services.

title: CBS News report questions USPS heat-safety program after Texas carrier's death
sum: A CBS News Texas I-Team investigation reviewed federal audits, OSHA records and USPS vehicle data after the death of Dallas mail carrier Eugene Gates Jr., whose medical examiner found hyperthermia contributed to his death. The report said records showed 10,337 of 18,153 active delivery vehicles in Texas lack air conditioning, and cited a USPS Office of Inspector General audit that found heat training was not always properly certified. USPS declined an interview; spokesperson Carol Hunt said in a statement that employee safety is a top priority and that the Heat Illness Prevention Program applies to all employees.
plain: No change to USPS rates or service. The report concerns heat-safety conditions for postal employees in Texas.

title: Amazon Prime Air starts drone deliveries in Chicago's south suburbs
sum: Amazon Prime Air drones are delivering packages in Chicago's south suburbs from the Amazon fulfillment center in Markham, CBS News reported. Amazon said each drone can reach up to 7.5 miles and carry up to 5 pounds, and that the site has 21 drones and 55 new positions. Residents raised noise and privacy concerns, and Amazon said onboard cameras are used only for navigation and obstacle detection.
plain: Customers within reach of the Markham center can now receive small packages of up to 5 pounds by drone, according to Amazon. Amazon said drivers continue to deliver all other packages.
tie: In August 2026, Amazon said Prime Air would start drone deliveries by the end of 2026 from sites near Chicago, Atlanta, Cleveland and Syracuse, N.Y.
new: Amazon's Chicago-area expansion has begun at the Markham site, with 21 drones in operation, while noise and privacy concerns and a Massachusetts lawmakers' letter to the FAA about Amazon's proposed plans there were reported; for shippers, this adds a delivery option for small items within 7.5 miles of the site.

title: Massachusetts lawmakers seek added review of Amazon Westborough drone hub
sum: Four members of the Massachusetts congressional delegation asked on October 14 for a site-specific environmental assessment and public comment before Amazon starts drone deliveries from a proposed Westborough hub, according to Dronelife. They requested written responses from Amazon and the FAA by October 29. The Zoning Board of Appeals hears a challenge to the project on November 2.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. Amazon's proposed Westborough drone hub still needs local approvals, and the lawmakers want added federal environmental review before operations begin.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach nearly 500 U.S. communities by the end of 2026.
new: Massachusetts lawmakers asked on October 14 for a site-specific environmental review of Amazon's Westborough hub, and a 15-state petition filed September 28 challenges the FAA's nationwide assessment; no shipper prices or service terms change yet, but the review could affect where Amazon's drone expansion proceeds.

title: Portland council votes to consider moratorium on drone delivery sites
sum: Portland City Council voted Wednesday, with 11 councilors in favor, to consider a moratorium on building facilities that support delivery drones, OPB reported. The step follows Amazon's land use permit application for a drone base at its North Portland warehouse; Amazon canceled a city permitting meeting on Tuesday, according to a city spokesperson.
plain: No change to rates or service now. A moratorium, if adopted, would pause drone facility development in Portland, and the city can vote on it in no fewer than 45 days.
why: Amazon's drone program operates in 11 U.S. cities, and a Portland pause on supporting facilities would affect its planned launch there next year.
new: Portland's council voted to consider a moratorium on drone support facilities, the first local restriction step in this storyline, and it comes as Amazon's Portland permit review is in question; the sources state no change to shipper prices or service.

title: Massachusetts Democrats ask FAA to review Amazon drone hub near Boston
sum: Four Massachusetts Democratic lawmakers wrote to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford on Oct. 14 asking for a new environmental review before an Amazon Prime Air hub is allowed in Westborough, about 30 miles west of Boston. They cited community concerns including noise, health and safety, and privacy. The FAA said it would respond directly, and Amazon did not immediately comment, according to Reuters.
plain: No change to rates or service. The lawmakers' request concerns whether the FAA should review the planned Westborough hub before it is allowed.
why: Local objections to a drone hub come as the FAA's July review lets qualifying operators launch fleets without a site-specific environmental analysis.
tie: Amazon said in August 2026 that Prime Air would reach almost 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026, up from 11 U.S. locations.
new: Four Massachusetts lawmakers asked the FAA on Oct. 14 for a new review of Amazon's planned Westborough hub, adding local pushback to the Sept. 28 suit by 15 states and Harris County, Texas; no change to shipper rates or service has been announced.

title: CrimsonLogic exec: importers need consistent customs data after de minimis
sum: In an opinion piece in Supply Chain Brain, Siddharth Priyesh of CrimsonLogic says importers must make sure information from suppliers, logistics providers and customs brokers is complete and consistent now that de minimis is suspended. The piece says the suspension was extended to shipments from all countries in August 2025 and that Congress has legislated repeal of the commercial shipment exemption from July 1, 2027.
plain: Formerly eligible shipments valued at $800 or less must follow the applicable Customs entry process and provide the required information. The author says the information may include a 10-digit Harmonized Tariff Schedule classification, Customs value and country of origin.

title: Happy Returns integrates with TikTok Shop for box-free returns
sum: UPS' Happy Returns is now integrated into TikTok Shop, according to Supply Chain Dive. Retailers on the platform can offer box- and label-free returns, with drop-off at 10,000 nationwide Return Bars. Everlane, Windsor and Pacsun are among the retailers using it.
plain: Retailers on TikTok Shop can now offer Happy Returns as a return method, and shoppers can drop items off at Return Bars without a box or label. Fulfilled by TikTok orders need no setup, while seller-fulfilled orders involve a setup process guided by Happy Returns.

title: Freight index projects record ground and express parcel rates in Q4
sum: A quarterly industry freight index released Oct. 13, 2026 projects the ground parcel rate per package at 43.3% above its January 2018 baseline in Q4, up 5.8% year over year. The express index is projected at 20.3%, up 13.8% year over year. The analysis ties the increases to fuel surcharges, peak fees and capacity limits. The analysis comes from investment bank TD Cowen and a parcel analytics firm, FreightWaves reported.
plain: According to the analysis, shippers face record ground and express parcel costs in Q4 2026. For packages in ZIP codes moved from extended to remote DAS, the fee rises to $17.75 when FedEx's rate increase takes effect on Jan. 4, 2027.
why: The analysis puts 2026 parcel rates at record highs and says fuel surcharge tables, not diesel prices, drove 72% of the surcharge rise since 2021.
new: An industry analysis projects the ground parcel index at 43.3% above its 2018 baseline and the express index at 20.3% in Q4, and says carrier table changes drove 72% of the fuel surcharge rise since 2021. Shippers now have a market-wide benchmark beyond the carrier-specific peak fees covered earlier.

title: NYC advocates urge passage of three last-mile delivery bills
sum: Labor union and environmental justice advocates, joined by city and state lawmakers, gathered in Red Hook to urge passage of the Delivery Protection Act, the Clean Deliveries Act and Intro 53, according to an Earthjustice release. The measures cover worker protections and warehouse pollution tied to last-mile delivery facilities, with Amazon the main target. The release says the Clean Deliveries Act has passed the State Senate three times and needs Assembly approval.
plain: No change to rates or service now; the three measures are proposed and have not passed. If enacted, they would change how delivery companies license facilities, employ drivers and manage warehouse emissions in New York.
why: The bills would regulate large last-mile warehouses and delivery contracting in New York City and State, where Amazon relies on thousands of workers, per Earthjustice.
new: Earthjustice's release gives the bills' provisions, including the Clean Deliveries Act's 50,000 sq. ft. mega-warehouse threshold and its three State Senate passages, and cites a 146% rise in truck-related crashes near facilities; it adds no change for shippers yet.

title: FedEx orders 2,000 electric trucks from Harbinger in $300M-plus deal
sum: FedEx ordered 2,000 all-electric trucks from EV startup Harbinger in a deal worth over $300 million, according to Environment America. The order is part of FedEx's effort to fully electrify its vehicle fleet by 2040. The group said the trucks are expected to cut emissions by 1.7 million tons and save $800 million in fuel costs over their life.
plain: No change to rates or service. The order concerns FedEx's own vehicle fleet.

title: Brokfill adds USPS final-mile delivery for fulfilled orders
sum: Broadscale Fulfillment LLC, operator of the Brokfill fulfillment platform, said on Oct. 13, 2026 that it has partnered with USPS to deliver orders to residential, rural and P.O. Box addresses nationwide. Brokfill said that in early testing with 15 clients, average delivery time to rural addresses dropped by 2 days.
plain: Brokfill clients, new and existing, can have eligible fulfilled orders routed to USPS for final delivery, including to P.O. Boxes, according to the company. No change to USPS rates or service for other shippers.

title: Diesel futures jump 20 cents in two hours on CME, FreightWaves reports
sum: Ultra-low sulfur diesel futures on the CME rose roughly 20 cents in about two hours Tuesday morning after briefly trading negative the day before, according to FreightWaves. FreightWaves energy markets analyst John Kingston said inventories have been drawn down and that prices could push back above $6 per gallon.
plain: No carrier has changed rates in this item. Kingston said the diesel move is a concern for anyone exposed to diesel costs, and he warned of possible further price increases.
new: Earlier coverage covered GOFO's 4% emergency fuel surcharge; this adds the roughly 20-cent futures jump and Kingston's view that depleted inventories and renewed Strait of Hormuz disruption could push diesel higher, though no new carrier surcharge is announced.

title: USPS recommends Dec. 17 Ground Advantage send-by date for the lower 48
sum: USPS announced its recommended 2026 holiday send-by dates on Sept. 22, and WSYR-TV repeated them in October. For delivery before Dec. 25 in the lower 48 states, Ground Advantage and First-Class items are to be sent by Dec. 17, Priority Mail by Dec. 18 and Priority Mail Express by Dec. 19. Ground Advantage to Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the territories should go by Dec. 16.
plain: Shippers using USPS face recommended send-by dates of Dec. 17 (Ground Advantage, First-Class), Dec. 18 (Priority Mail) and Dec. 19 (Priority Mail Express) for delivery before Dec. 25 in the lower 48 states. No change to rates is reported.

USPS Ground Advantage deadline for AK, HI, PR, territories
USPS Ground Advantage and First-Class deadline, lower 48
USPS Priority Mail deadline, lower 48
USPS Priority Mail Express deadline, lower 48

title: Analysis: 2026 peak shipping season starts earlier and spreads over more weeks
sum: In an analysis published 13 October 2026 in Global Trade Magazine, author Tomasz Jeleń says shippers are moving goods earlier and shipments are spread more evenly across sea, air and warehousing. He cites about 60% of sea sailings on schedule, a 29% rise in China–Europe trains in the first quarter, and a nearly 33% year-on-year fall in low-value air shipments after the EU's 1 July customs change.
plain: No carrier price or service change is announced. The piece is the author's view that shippers are shipping earlier, and it says freight rates have risen on some lanes.

title: Earthjustice analyst urges New York action on Amazon delivery
sum: In an opinion piece in City Limits, Sasan Saadat, a senior research and policy analyst at Earthjustice, argues that Amazon and other e-commerce delivery vehicles have worsened traffic, air quality and safety in New York City. He cites 3,602 tickets for blocking bus lanes and transit routes and 2,162 for speeding in school zones over four years. He urges the City Council to pass the Delivery Protection Act and the Assembly to pass a state warehouse emissions bill.
plain: No change to rates or service. The piece is one author's view and advocates for proposed city and state legislation that has not been enacted.

title: Burq outlines staged-autonomy model for delivery-routing AI
sum: Burq cofounder Salman Habib told FreightWaves the company's delivery-decision software earns authority one segment at a time, such as parcel, LTL or gig. Habib and cofounder Shaban Habib set out the approach Oct. 13 in a paper called "Earned Autonomy."
plain: No change to rates or service. Burq described how retailers can trial its AI in a read-only Shadow mode before it makes live decisions.
why: Burq's software picks among fleets, gig, parcel, LTL and drones for retailers' orders, and the paper sets how much authority its AI gets over those choices.
syn: Burq, whose software chooses how each retailer order is delivered, laid out an "Earned Autonomy" doctrine on Oct. 13, according to cofounder Salman Habib in an interview with FreightWaves. Under it, AI starts each segment, such as parcel, LTL or gig, with no authority and moves up four rungs (Manual, Shadow, Review, Autonomous) on evidence from live orders. Habib said the retailer sets the promotion bar, for example 90% agreement with dispatchers, and a rule breach demotes a segment automatically. Every decision is logged in a Decision Ledger that customers can export as a CSV file.

aff.what: Can start in Shadow mode, where the AI reads decisions and reports after 30, 60 or 90 days, Habib said.
Approve each step; the retailer sets the bar, such as 90% agreement, for full autonomy.
Can choose own-data-only use or opt in to anonymized network-wide performance data, Habib said.

title: Walmart adds eight carriers to approved list for seller-fulfilled orders
sum: Walmart Marketplace said Oct. 13 that sellers fulfilling their own orders may now use eight more parcel carriers: UniUni, SpeedX, Exelot, SwiftX, TForce Final Mile, Gofo, OSM Worldwide and DoorDash. Metropolitan Warehouse & Delivery is also available for freight shipments, according to Supply Chain Dive.
plain: Walmart Marketplace sellers who ship their own orders can now use eight more approved parcel carriers. Walmart's top preferred carriers remain the Postal Service, FedEx and UPS, and shipping with a non-approved carrier may lead to suppression, suspension or termination.
why: Sellers on Walmart's marketplace gain more carrier choices, and the retailer says non-approved carriers risk suppression, suspension or termination.

title: Westborough ZBA to hear Amazon drone pad appeal Nov. 2; town meeting votes on bylaw
sum: Westborough, Massachusetts, will hold a Zoning Board of Appeals hearing on Monday, Nov. 2 at 7:05 p.m. on residents' appeal against Amazon's Prime Air drone launch pad at 64 Otis Street, according to a town agenda posted Oct. 9. The Planning Board voted Oct. 6 to continue the site plan hearing to Nov. 10 at Amazon's request, and a Special Town Meeting on Oct. 19 takes up a new bylaw on unmanned aircraft.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. Amazon's planned drone launch pad in Westborough remains under local review, and the town page says the company is still seeking site-specific FAA approvals.
tie: The hearing follows DroneXL's October 2026 reports that the Westborough launch hinged on a zoning appeal and that the Planning Board voted Oct. 6 to continue the site plan to Nov. 10.
new: Westborough has set the Nov. 2 zoning appeal hearing and scheduled an Oct. 19 town meeting vote on a drone bylaw, after Amazon asked for its Planning Board hearing to wait; this does not change prices or service for shippers.

title: SHIP.com CEO says platforms should embed shipping for AI-led peak
sum: In an opinion piece, SHIP.com founder and CEO Joe DiSorbo argues that AI-driven shopping has sped up the front end of commerce while independent sellers' shipping work stays manual. He cites Visa Acceptance Solutions' 2026 index, in which 47% of online shoppers used AI in their latest purchase, and a Bringg study in which 51% of US shoppers would abandon a purchase without an on-time delivery estimate.
plain: No change to rates or service. The article is an opinion on how commerce platforms could build rate comparison, address validation, batch processing and tracking alerts into seller workflows.
why: The piece, from a shipping software vendor's CEO, frames shipping automation for independent marketplace sellers as a holiday 2026 issue, citing Visa and Bringg survey figures.

title: Survey: 37% of Sri Lankan e-commerce exporters lack full de minimis awareness
sum: An ODI Global report, 'E-commerce and international trade in Sri Lanka', found that 27% of surveyed e-commerce exporters are not aware of de minimis and a further 10% are unsure, The Morning reported. Among non-e-commerce exporters, only 32% were aware of the threshold benefits. The findings rest on a survey of 953 exporters and importers.
plain: No change to rates or service. The report says gaps in de minimis knowledge may limit how Sri Lankan exporters set prices, choose markets and plan shipping for direct-to-consumer sales.

title: GOFO adds 4% emergency fuel surcharge from Oct. 26
sum: GOFO will apply a 4% emergency fuel surcharge to base delivery rates across all U.S. regions from Oct. 26, 2026, according to a notice to partners described in an industry analysis. GOFO said U.S. on-highway diesel prices have risen about 40% since July. The carrier is not adding peak surcharges this year.
plain: Shippers sending volume through GOFO pay 4% more on base delivery rates from Oct. 26, 2026. The surcharge stays while the national diesel average is above $5.46 per gallon, and GOFO has said it will add no peak surcharges.
tie: The industry analysis notes that the UPS international air import fuel surcharge reached 47.75% in September, citing the same fuel market.

dates.w: UPS and Amazon Shipping begin per-package residential demand fees
GOFO 4% emergency fuel surcharge takes effect; FedEx demand fees begin

title: FedEx Europe launches online portal for temperature-controlled pharma shipments
sum: FedEx Europe has launched an online portal for pharmaceutical and life sciences shippers to book and manage temperature-controlled shipments in 26 European markets. The portal gives access to FedEx Temp-Assure Advantage and was introduced ahead of the year-end peak season. FedEx told Air Cargo News the offering covers air and road transport for consignments of up to 68 kg, according to IndexBox.
plain: Pharma and life sciences shippers in the 26 covered European markets can onboard, order pre-conditioned packaging, schedule shipments and manage returns online for non-freight domestic and intra-European moves. The sources state no change to rates or fees.

title: FedEx closes Calverton, N.Y., facility under Network 2.0 consolidation
sum: FedEx has permanently closed its Edwards Avenue facility in Calverton, N.Y., as part of its Network 2.0 strategy, spokesperson David Westrick said in an emailed statement. Package drop-off for customers who used the site moves to the Middle Island, N.Y., location, according to Westrick.
plain: Customers who dropped off packages at the Calverton site can use the FedEx location at 750 Middle Country Rd. in Middle Island, N.Y. No change to rates was stated.
tie: The closure follows the April 2023 plan to consolidate Express, Ground and the services division into Federal Express Corporation, which took effect June 1, 2024, according to company filings cited in the article.

title: GLS US launches GLS Connect digital shipping platform
sum: GLS US, a regional parcel carrier serving the Western U.S. and Texas, announced GLS Connect on October 12, 2026. The platform combines domestic and international shipping, tracking, reporting, pickup scheduling and account and billing tools in one portal. GLS said customers can begin using it now via "Try the New Portal" on the GLS website login screen.
plain: GLS customers can switch to the new GLS Connect portal now, and existing address books, billing information, account settings and available shipment history carry over. The announcement states no change to rates or fees.

title: FedEx adds duty and tax payments to Import Tool in Asia Pacific
sum: FedEx added an integrated duty and tax payment function to the FedEx Import Tool and expanded where the tool is available, according to a company release cited by PYMNTS. The tool is now offered in Australia, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea and Thailand.
plain: Importers in the listed Asia Pacific countries can pay duties and taxes through the FedEx Import Tool. The release does not state any change to rates or fees.
why: Importers in nine Asia Pacific markets can now pay duties and taxes inside the FedEx clearance tool, per the release.
tie: FedEx first launched the FedEx Import Tool in Australia, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan in October 2024.

title: Class action accuses Google, UPS of sharing tracking data
sum: A proposed class action filed Friday accuses Alphabet-owned Google LLC and United Parcel Service of America Inc. of invasion of privacy, wiretapping and other claims, according to the Daily Journal. The complaint alleges a "Package Tracking System" shared consumers' browsing activity, location information and other personal data with advertising and technology companies despite promising privacy.
plain: No change to UPS rates or service. The suit is a proposed class action, and its claims are allegations that have not been decided by a court.

title: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe partner on SMB financing, payments
sum: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe announced a long-term collaboration, reported by The Paypers on 12 October 2026, to widen financing access for small and medium-sized businesses that ship with FedEx. The first joint solution is scheduled to launch in early 2027, and FedEx will also use Stripe as one of its payment processing options, adding more than 50 payment methods.
plain: No change to shipping rates or service. FedEx SMB customers are expected to get a financing option through Stripe Capital from early 2027, and FedEx will add more than 50 payment methods through Stripe, according to the companies.

title: Northglenn, Colorado weighs special-use permit rules for drone delivery hubs
sum: Northglenn, Colorado, held a first reading on October 12 of an ordinance that would require a one-year special-use permit for drone delivery hubs, with a second reading set for October 26, Dronelife reported. Salem, Oregon's City Council also voted on October 12 to study what regulations it could impose.
plain: No change to rates or service today. If Northglenn's council approves the ordinance, operators wanting a drone hub there would need a one-year special-use permit meeting the stated limits.
why: Local zoning rules could shape where drone delivery hubs are sited as Wing and Walmart plan Denver-area service next year, while the FAA keeps control of the airspace.
new: Northglenn, Colorado, has a drone hub ordinance in readings (second reading October 26) and Salem, Oregon, voted to study options; this adds local ground-level rules alongside federal airspace oversight, with no change yet to shipper rates or service.

title: Gastonia notifies residents of Walmart drone deliveries at Myrtle School Road store
sum: Walmart has finished a drone delivery site at its Supercenter at 223 N. Myrtle School Road in Gastonia, North Carolina, and the city issued a notice on why drones may fly over nearby neighborhoods, DroneXL reported citing WSOC-TV. The aircraft will serve eligible customers within about 6 miles of the store; no start date or flight count was given.
plain: Eligible Walmart customers within about 6 miles of the Gastonia store will be able to receive drone deliveries; no start date has been reported. No change to rates or service terms has been announced.
tie: Walmart and Wing said on Oct. 5, 2026 that they would add Denver and Seattle in 2027, expanding a partnership that the source says already counts Charlotte among metros now served.
new: Walmart finished a drone site at its Gastonia, North Carolina store, which the city announced to residents; the FAA review covering the area allows up to 400 deliveries a day per hub, though no start date was given.

title: Federal agents raid Kansas City USPS center, arrest several employees
sum: More than 80 agents from five agencies, led by the USPS Office of Inspector General, carried out an operation at the USPS distribution center at 1700 Cleveland Ave. in Kansas City on the evening of Sept. 9, according to the OIG as reported by FOX4 and the North Platte Bulletin. The OIG said several employees were arrested within two hours and a stolen firearm was recovered. The report ran alongside customer complaints of mail delays in Kansas City and Omaha.
plain: No change to rates or service. Customers in the Kansas City and Omaha areas have reported delayed or misrouted mail, and the sources do not link the delays to the raid.
tie: The report follows a 2025 USPS Inspector General audit of the Omaha facility, cited in a March 12 letter from Sen. Pete Ricketts, and the OIG's 2024 audit of the local Postal Service.
new: The USPS OIG confirmed a Sept. 9 operation at the Kansas City distribution center that led to employee arrests, and local customers and Sen. Ricketts' March letter point to delays; no change to rates or service standards was announced for shippers.

title: Walmart opens 900,000-sq-ft automated fulfillment center in Stockton, California
sum: Walmart opened a more than 900,000-square-foot fulfillment center in Stockton, California, according to an Oct. 8 press release cited by Supply Chain Dive. It is the retailer's fifth next-generation fulfillment center. The site uses a high-density storage and retrieval system that cuts the 12-step fulfillment process to five steps.
plain: No change to rates or service. The facility adds Walmart fulfillment capacity serving West Coast customers.
tie: Walmart first announced plans for the next-generation fulfillment centers in 2022, when it said they could provide 75% of the U.S. population with next- or two-day shipping.

title: USPS suspends mail delivery and retail service in 60 Northwest Florida ZIP codes
sum: The USPS Florida 1 District said on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, that it suspended mail delivery and retail services in 60 ZIP codes in Northwest Florida after severe weather tied to Hurricane Isaias. The suspension took effect immediately, and USPS has not given a reopening date.
plain: Mail and package delivery and post office retail services are suspended in the 60 affected ZIP codes, and USPS has given no date for resuming them. USPS said no alternative postal locations are available for affected customers.

title: Orlando trucking owner pleads guilty in $1M USPS Freight Auction fraud
sum: Khayyam Arif Oglu Farajov, 40, owner of Talishco LLC in Orlando, pleaded guilty to one wire fraud count and one money laundering count, federal prosecutors announced Friday. DOJ said he falsely marked USPS Freight Auction shipments as delivered and collected more than $1 million. He agreed to forfeit two seized brokerage accounts and pay $993,979 in restitution, and the court has not scheduled sentencing.
plain: No change to USPS rates or service. The case concerns payments to a supplier in the USPS Freight Auction bulk-mail trucking program.
tie: DOJ announced the indictment in March 2026, and a 2024 federal audit of USPS Freight Auction proof-of-delivery controls covered the same period as the scheme.

title: ShipStation adds Ship with Walmart rates and $100 lost-package cover
sum: ShipStation announced Ship with Walmart, giving Walmart Marketplace sellers access to Walmart-negotiated shipping rates inside its platform, plus up to $100 in protection on lost-item claims for eligible orders shipped on time. The service covers U.S. domestic shipments only. ShipStation's blog says rates may be as much as 60% below the market rate.
plain: Walmart Marketplace sellers on ShipStation can buy Walmart-negotiated labels alongside their existing carrier accounts, with up to $100 of lost-item protection on eligible on-time orders. It applies to U.S. domestic shipments only.
why: Walmart Marketplace sellers using ShipStation get another rate option for U.S. domestic parcels, though savings depend on each seller's own lanes and weights.

title: OnTrac posts 2026 rate, AHS/LPS and area surcharge ZIP files on its rates page
sum: OnTrac's own Surcharges and rates page now lists four newly posted PDF files: 2026 rates, 2026 AHS and LPS rates, an area surcharge ZIP code list and a 2024 rates file.
plain: OnTrac's Surcharges and rates page now links four PDF documents that were not previously listed: a 2026 rates file, a 2026 file covering AHS and LPS rates, an area surcharge ZIP code list and a 2024 rates file. This was posted on the carrier's own page. The change shows only the file links, not their contents, so any price, surcharge or effective-date changes in the documents are not visible here. The 2024 file may be an archived guide rather than a new one.

title: Zipline launches drone delivery in Round Rock, Texas
sum: Zipline has launched drone delivery in Round Rock, Texas, its first site in the Austin area, KABB reported. Customers within about three miles of the site can order through the Zipline app, which lists 25 participating businesses. Zipline said it has had no serious injuries after more than 135 million commercial autonomous miles.
plain: Customers within about three miles of the Zipline site can order from participating businesses by drone. No change to parcel carrier rates or service.
why: Zipline's first Austin-area site adds a drone option for local merchants, with plans for more sites across the metro, according to the company's community engagement lead.
new: KABB reports Zipline's Round Rock service lists 25 participating businesses within about three miles of the site, and the company plans more sites across the Austin metro; this does not change rates or service for most parcel shippers.

title: CWU pauses further rollout of Royal Mail's Delivery Model 26
sum: The Communication Workers Union announced a pause to any further rollout of Royal Mail's Delivery Model 26 (DM26). The union is calling for an agreed plan to address delivery offices where the new working arrangements are not operating as intended.
plain: No change to rates or prices. The union's pause applies to further rollout of DM26 at Royal Mail delivery offices; no new dates were given in the source.

title: Costco CEO cites faster big-item and same-day delivery times
sum: Costco CEO Ron Vachris said on the fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call that delivery of furnishings and appliances has fallen from four to five weeks to three and four days over five years. He said most same-day deliveries are completed within 45 minutes, according to TheStreet via AOL.com. The retailer has also expanded delivery partnerships with DoorDash and Uber Eats.
plain: No change to rates or service for parcel shippers. The item describes Costco's own delivery speeds for members.

title: UniUni responds to Tacoma complaints of packages left at wrong addresses
sum: KIRO 7 reported that several Tacoma residents, particularly in North and West Tacoma, said UniUni packages marked delivered did not arrive at their addresses. UniUni said the practices described are not consistent with its standards and that it is speaking with local delivery service providers. A group of neighbors has filed complaints with the Washington Attorney General's office, according to the report.
plain: No change to UniUni rates or service terms. Shippers using UniUni in the Tacoma area may see delivery-confirmation problems like those residents described.

title: Amazon seeks approval for about 1,000 daily drone deliveries from North Haven, CT
sum: Connecticut's Department of Energy and Environmental Protection is taking public comments on Amazon's plan for drone deliveries from its North Haven warehouse, CT News Junkie reported. Amazon seeks about 1,000 daily deliveries within 7.5 miles, and told lawmakers it expects deliveries to start in spring 2027. Comments are open until Oct. 15.
plain: No change to rates or service yet. If approved, Amazon would offer opt-in drone delivery within 30 minutes for packages of 5 pounds or less to addresses within 7.5 miles of the North Haven warehouse, with a stated start of spring 2027.

title: UPS to report Q3 earnings Oct. 27; analysts expect $1.63 per share
sum: UPS is expected to report fiscal third-quarter 2026 earnings before the market opens on Oct. 27, according to Barchart via Yahoo Finance. Analysts expect diluted EPS of $1.63, down 6.3% from $1.74 a year earlier. For the full year they expect $7.21, compared with $7.16 in fiscal 2025.
plain: No change to rates or service. The item previews earnings expectations and does not announce any price or service change for shippers.

title: Dollar General expands Instacart same-day delivery at in-store prices
sum: Dollar General is expanding same-day delivery through Instacart and letting customers pay the same product prices online as in its stores, according to a Yahoo Finance article. The service initially covers about 7,000 locations, with plans to reach roughly 20,000 stores this fall.
plain: Dollar General customers ordering through Instacart pay in-store product prices, and coverage is set to grow from about 7,000 to roughly 20,000 stores this fall. No change to parcel carrier rates or service.

title: India Post and Blue Dart sign nationwide parcel services agreement
sum: The Department of Posts and Blue Dart Express Limited signed an agreement in New Delhi on October 9 to collaborate on India Post Parcel services. Blue Dart will gain access to the Department's network of 1.64 lakh post offices, according to the report.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The agreement covers prepaid and cash-on-delivery parcels with OTP-based delivery authentication and real-time tracking, with no start date or pricing stated.

title: PRC notes three USPS competitive contract filings; comments due Oct. 20
sum: The Postal Regulatory Commission noticed three Postal Service filings on competitive negotiated service agreements, each accepted October 9, 2026. They cover an extension of an international service contract and requests to add two domestic contracts to the Competitive product list. Comments are due October 20, 2026.
plain: No change to published rates or service for shippers. The notice covers individual negotiated agreements, with public comment open until October 20, 2026.
why: The filings add or extend negotiated rate contracts for Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage, which are competitive products used by parcel shippers.

title: Stord closes $400M Citi-led credit facility, names CFO and CRO
sum: Stord said Thursday it closed a $400 million credit facility led by Citi, which it said was oversubscribed at nearly double its original target. The Atlanta-based fulfillment company also hired Bill Zerella as chief financial officer and Mark Wayland as chief revenue officer. Stord said the facility and its May $250 million Series F bring 2026 equity and credit capacity to $650 million.
plain: No change to rates or service. Stord said it will use the capital to expand its fulfillment network, deploy more robotics and invest in AI.
tie: The facility follows a $250 million Series F led by Strike Capital in May that valued Stord at $3 billion, according to the article.

title: Chicago residents sue Coco, Serve over delivery robot biometric data
sum: Two Chicago residents filed proposed class-action lawsuits in Cook County on Oct. 9 alleging robots run by Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics captured facial and hand measurements without consent, Digital Trends reported, citing The Associated Press. Both companies have denied the allegations. The suits cite Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act.
plain: No change to rates or service. The allegations have not been decided in court.
why: The suits test how Illinois biometric law applies to sidewalk delivery robots, which operate under a Chicago pilot set to expire in May 2027.
syn: Two Chicago residents filed proposed class-action lawsuits in Cook County on Oct. 9 alleging that delivery robots run by Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics captured their facial and hand measurements without consent, according to Digital Trends, citing The Associated Press. The complaints invoke Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act and say cameras and LiDAR sensors gathered the data. Both companies have denied the claims. The outcome could affect how delivery robots collect, store and share data, and Chicago's pilot program for the machines is set to expire in May 2027 unless renewed.

title: USPS lengthens delivery standards for Priority Mail, Ground Advantage to and from Hawaii
sum: The U.S. Postal Service has released new delivery expectations for mail to and from Hawaii, according to Hawaii Public Radio. Priority Mail moves from two to three days to two to four days, and Ground Advantage moves from two to five days to at least 10 days.
plain: Shippers sending Priority Mail to or from Hawaii should expect two to four days instead of two to three. Ground Advantage packages are now expected to take at least 10 days instead of two to five. The source gives no effective date or rate change.

title: Zipline opens Round Rock drone delivery as FAA Austin comment window runs
sum: Zipline opened drone delivery in the Austin area on October 9 through its First Flight early-access program in Round Rock, Texas, open to the first 5,000 residents who sign up. The FAA's draft environmental assessment for Zipline's Austin operations remains open for public comment until October 11. The draft sets an Austin ceiling of 30 Chargers, 600 Dropbox kiosks and 30,000 deliveries a day across 2,498 square miles, DroneXL reported.
plain: Customers within 3 miles of 3000 E. Palm Valley Blvd. in Round Rock can order from the Zipline app, with a delivery weight limit of about 5 pounds reported. Early-access members get $10 off their first three orders and no service or delivery fees. No change to rates or service for other shippers.
tie: DroneXL reports Zipline began flying in Houston's Cypress area on April 29 and named Austin as its next Texas market in June 2026.
new: Zipline started Round Rock deliveries on October 9, with the FAA comment period closing October 11; the draft would cap Austin at 30,000 deliveries a day, and the item adds a Zipline Texas launch to the expansion news from Wing and Walmart.

title: FCC to vote Oct. 29 on lifting 800 MHz cellular ban for drones
sum: The FCC will vote on October 29, 2026 on a draft order that exempts drones from the airborne ban in the 800 MHz Cellular band, Chairman Brendan Carr announced on October 7. The draft says the ban began as a 1984 policy and was codified in 1991 for airplane phones. If adopted, the rule takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication.
plain: No change to shipper rates or service now. If adopted, drones could use the band for networked operations, including last-mile delivery, which the draft names among its use cases.
tie: The FCC first asked about dropping the ban in January 2023 and revisited it in the April 2026 public notice DA 26-314, according to DroneXL.

dates.w: FCC votes on draft order opening 800 MHz band to drones

title: Lowe's starts Wing and DoorDash drone delivery pilot in Matthews, NC
sum: Lowe's has launched a drone delivery pilot at its Matthews, North Carolina store, according to Unmanned Airspace. The service aims to deliver orders in 20 minutes and runs with Wing and DoorDash, which already operate drone delivery in the Charlotte area.
plain: Lowe's customers near the Matthews, North Carolina store can get eligible orders by drone, with a stated goal of 20 minutes. No change to rates or service for other shippers.
tie: Wing also announced an expansion with Walmart to Denver and Seattle in 2027, as covered in October 2026.
new: Lowe's has started a drone delivery pilot in Matthews, North Carolina with Wing and DoorDash, adding a home improvement retailer to the drone delivery sites reported earlier; shippers see no change in rates, and the service covers small items of about 2.5 pounds.

title: Google, UPS face California privacy class action over package tracking box
sum: Two California residents, Lennie Woodley and Joseph Schrant, filed a class-action privacy complaint against Google and UPS in the Northern District of California, according to MediaPost. They allege a package-tracking box on a Google search page sends user data to outside companies beyond the tracking number. Google and UPS had not responded to MediaPost's request for comment.
plain: No change to rates or service. The complaint is a pending lawsuit and none of its allegations have been decided.
why: The suit targets a Google tracking feature tied to UPS, which could affect how consumers' tracking lookups handle data.

title: UPS adds RFID tracking and PIN delivery for holiday peak, plans ~100,000 hires
sum: UPS entered the holiday season in early October 2026 with plans to hire about 100,000 seasonal workers and new services: RFID-powered tracking, Protected Delivery PIN verification for high-value parcels, expanded pickup visibility, Happy Returns returns, Roadie same-day and bulky delivery, and limited-edition holiday packaging. The Yahoo Finance analysis, which frames the news for investors, ties the additions to the UPS Secure Commerce suite launched in late September 2026.
plain: Shippers using UPS have access to new tracking, delivery-verification, returns and same-day or bulky delivery options for the holiday season. The article does not state any price or fee change.
tie: The services are bundled with the UPS Secure Commerce suite, which the article says launched in late September 2026 and combines InsureShield, Parcel Pro and CommerceShield.

title: Amazon cuts single-use plastic share of North American shipments to 27%
sum: Amazon said the share of its North American shipments using single-use plastic packaging fell from 65% in 2023 to 27% in 2025, according to an AP report. About 11% of its global orders ship in original manufacturer packaging, the company said. Amazon is also rolling out 30-minute delivery in a growing number of cities this year.
plain: No change to rates or service is announced. Amazon is lighter and less boxed in its packaging, and 30-minute delivery is being rolled out in a growing number of cities.

title: Shipt names Raj Kapoor CEO, effective Oct. 18, 2026
sum: Shipt announced that Raj Kapoor will rejoin the company as CEO effective Oct. 18, 2026. He succeeds Kamau Witherspoon, who has led Shipt for more than four years and will remain in his role through late October. Kapoor was Shipt's COO from 2022 to 2025 and has been senior vice president of marketplace at Target since 2025.
plain: No change to rates or service. The announcement covers a leadership change at Shipt, a Target subsidiary that offers same-day delivery and Target Last Mile Delivery.

title: USPS files to add international service contract 128 to competitive list
sum: The Postal Service said it filed a request with the Postal Regulatory Commission on October 8, 2026 to add a Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International & First-Class Package International Service contract (Contract 128) to the Competitive Product List. The Federal Register notice is dated October 15, 2026 and cites Docket Nos. MC2027-4 and K2027-4.
plain: No change to published rates or service for most shippers. The filing adds one negotiated international contract to the Mail Classification Schedule, pending Postal Regulatory Commission review.
why: Negotiated service agreements set contract terms for individual customers, so the filing covers a single agreement rather than published rates for all shippers.

title: Connecticut man gets 2 years for $3.5M Amazon Relay fraud scheme
sum: Ameer Nasir, 25, of Trumbull, Connecticut, was sentenced to 24 months in federal prison plus three years of supervised release, FreightWaves reported. Prosecutors linked 23 trucking accounts he registered with Amazon Logistics to more than 1,000 trailer movements that never occurred. The court ordered $3,547,090.93 in restitution, and he must report to prison Nov. 12.
plain: No change to rates or service. The case concerns past fraud on Amazon's Relay trucking platform, which ran from December 2019 through February 2021.

dates.w: Nasir must report to federal prison

title: CBP proposes earlier filing deadlines for low-value imports, postal entries
sum: U.S. Customs and Border Protection proposed in an Oct. 8 Federal Register filing that entry type 11 imports be filed on or before arrival rather than within 15 days, and that postal entry type 13 require more data. Public comments are due Dec. 7.
plain: If adopted, importers of goods valued at $2,500 or less would face earlier filing deadlines and additional data requirements. CBP said the changes would result in higher shipping costs for imports under both entry types; no effective date is stated.

dates.w: Public comment deadline on CBP low-value import proposal

title: Amazon targets 5,000 drivers in smart glasses by end of 2026
sum: Amazon aims to have 5,000 delivery drivers wearing AI smart glasses by the end of 2026 and more than 20,000 by the end of 2027, according to a Bloomberg opinion piece by Dave Lee that cites Amazon executive Viraj Chatterjee. Amazon says the glasses track a driver's shift from start to finish, give hands-free guidance and are meant to speed deliveries and cut errors. Lee wrote that the company risks another privacy controversy.
plain: No change to rates, fees or service terms for shippers. The item concerns equipment for Amazon's own delivery drivers.

title: Canada Post works to resume EU parcel shipping before holiday season
sum: Canada Post said it is working on solutions to resume personal and business shipping to the EU ahead of the Christmas season. It paused package delivery to nine EU countries, including France and Germany, on July 1 after the EU changed its customs and import VAT rules.
plain: Canada Post parcel delivery to nine EU countries remains suspended while the carrier seeks a compliant approach. Regular letter mail is not affected.

title: CBP starts processing IEEPA tariff refunds for finally liquidated entries
sum: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has begun processing some finally liquidated entries from plaintiffs the Court of International Trade ruled entitled to refunds of IEEPA tariffs, according to an Oct. 6 court filing. CBP has accepted 477 CAPE declarations covering 425,517 entries, and the capability is expected to handle roughly $11.4 billion, or 6.9%, of IEEPA tariffs.
plain: Importers that sued for refunds and submitted a valid importer of record number to CBP by July 30, 2026, can now apply through the CAPE portal for refunds on finally liquidated entries. Plaintiffs that submitted a number after July 30 must await further CBP instructions, with no timeframe given.
tie: CBP had targeted the end of July for this third phase of its CAPE rollout but delayed implementation until October, per Supply Chain Dive.

title: Drivers file overtime suits against FedEx in federal courts nationwide
sum: More than 200 drivers filed nearly identical suits in South Carolina last week, including 38 in Charleston federal court on Oct. 8-9, alleging FedEx owes them overtime under the Fair Labor Standards Act. The drivers' lead attorney said FedEx faces roughly 10,000 individual suits across every federal district. FedEx said on Oct. 15 that its service providers must comply with wage and hour laws for their employees.
plain: No change to rates or service has been announced. The suits concern overtime pay for drivers employed by FedEx's contracted service providers.
why: The suits challenge the independent service provider model FedEx uses for delivery drivers, with roughly 10,000 cases in every federal district, per the drivers' attorney.
tie: A Pennsylvania court ruled in May that the drivers could not sue FedEx together in a nationwide class action, according to the article, which led to the one-by-one filings.

title: Amazon Prime Air adds Tracy, Calif., in 500-city drone delivery expansion
sum: Amazon is adding Tracy, Calif., to Prime Air drone delivery as part of a 500-city U.S. expansion, according to an announcement reported by the Tracy Press. Service from the East Grant Line Road fulfillment center is to begin within the next few months, covering packages up to five pounds within a 7.5-mile radius.
plain: Amazon customers near the Tracy fulfillment center are to be able to choose drone delivery for eligible items of five pounds or less within the next few months. Amazon said delivery is free for Prime members on orders over $50, $2.99 for Prime members on orders under $50 and $4.99 for non-Prime members.
new: Amazon said it is adding Tracy to a 500-city Prime Air expansion, with fees of $2.99 to $4.99 on smaller orders, so shippers and retailers in the area face another drone delivery competitor operating under existing waivers or certificates.

title: UPS routed F-35 parts through Hong Kong in error, Bloomberg reports
sum: UPS mistakenly routed sensitive components from Lockheed Martin's F-35 fighter through Hong Kong, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, as summarized by Seeking Alpha. An employee failed to see a warning that the shipment was subject to U.S. arms-export restrictions, according to the report.
plain: No change to rates or service for shippers. The report concerns a routing error on a single restricted defense shipment.
